subject: DISASTER MANAGEMENT
content_markdown:
Disaster Stats
- **Internal displacements due to natural disasters:** 5.4 million displacements in India in 2024, the highest in 12 years ([IDMC GRID 2025](https://www.internal-displacement.org/global-report/grid2025/)); South Asia recorded over 4.6 million disaster displacements in 2025 out of 29.9 million globally ([IDMC GRID 2026](https://api.internal-displacement.org/sites/default/files/2026-05/IDMC-GRID-2026-Global-Report-on-Internal-Displacement.pdf))

• Droughts
        - **Impact:** 40% land area and 70 % of cultivable area prone to droughts
        - **Vulnerability:** Affect 40% of population
        - 60% increase in droughts in last 25 years

• Earthquakes
        - [[Data by NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf)]
- **Vulnerability:** ~59-60% of landmass is prone to earthquakes (80% of population) ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf))
        - **Unsustainable infra:** 90% casualties due to collapse of houses & structures

• Landslide
- 12.6% of land area is prone to landslides ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf) / [GSI](https://www.gsi.gov.in/)).

• Floods
- **Area:** 12% of land area (over 40 million hectares) prone to floods and river erosion ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf))
        - **Vulnerable sections:** Children and women, constitute 85% of death.
        - **Economic Losses:** average annual loss is estimated to be US$ 7.4 billion

• Urban fire
        - **Hotspots:** Maha & Guj accounts 30% of India’s fire accident deaths
        - **Reasons:** 60% of Fire related deaths occur in Residential buildings.
        - **Shortcomings:** 65% shortage of fire stations.
        - **Impact:** 4th biggest risk to business continuity (India Risk Survey 2021)
        - **Loss of life:** 35 people killed every day due to fire related incidents
        - **Vulnerable section:** 60% of those killed are women

• Heatwave
        - **Coverage:** 90% of India is in a “danger zone” from it ([PLOS Climate](https://journals.plos.org/climate/article?id=10.1371/journal.pclm.0000161)).
        - **Financial loss:** $2,500 billion by 2030 (Globally)
        - **Heat stress loss in India:** 6% of its working hours equivalent to 35 Million fulltime jobs ([ILO](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/@dgreports/@dcomm/@publ/documents/publication/wcms_711919.pdf))
        - **Loss of life:** 155,937 heat-related deaths in India in 2021 (Global Burden of Disease study)

• Forest Fire
        - **Causes:** Only 4% natural causes globally ([MoEFCC](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100))
- **Vulnerability:** >35% (~36%) of India's forest cover is prone to frequent forest fires ([FSI](https://fsi.nic.in/uploads/isfr2023/isfr_book_eng-vol-1_2023.pdf) / [ISFR 2023](https://fsi.nic.in/uploads/isfr2023/isfr_book_eng-vol-1_2023.pdf)).
        - **Carbon emission:** 2.5 billion to 4.0 billion tons annually ([IPCC](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/))
        - **Global:** Amazon forest **–** 8000 incidents in 2019

• Cyclones
        - **Exposure:** India exposed to 10% of world’s tropical cyclones.
- **Extent:** ~75% (5,700 km) of India's 7,516.6 km coastline (revised to 11,098.8 km in Dec 2024) prone to cyclones and tsunamis ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf)).
        - **Vulnerability:** 8% of area and 1/3rd of Indians are vulnerable to cyclone

subject: INDIAN ECONOMY
content_markdown:
GENERAL STATE OF ECONOMY (ECONOMIC SURVEY 2024-25)

• Global Growth
- **IMF Projections** -> 3.2% and 3.3% for 2024 and 2025, respectively ([IMF WEO](https://www.imf.org/en/Publications/WEO) / [Economic Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)).
            - Over the next 5 years → average 3.2%.

• Resilient Domestic Economy
- **GDP Growth:** Real GDP grew by 6.5% in FY25 (6.7% in Q1, 5.4% in Q2 FY25) and is estimated to grow by 7.4% in FY26 (FAE), with FY27 projected at 6.8–7.2% ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **GVA Growth:** Real Gross Value Added (GVA) is estimated to grow by 7.3% in FY26 (FAE), up from 6.4% in FY25 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **Primary Sector:** Agricultural growth rebounded to 3.8% in FY25 (4.4% 5-year average; 3.5% in Q2 FY26) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **Secondary Sector:** Industry GVA grew by 7.0% in H1 FY26 (Manufacturing GVA grew 7.72% in Q1 and 9.13% in Q2 FY26), up from 6.2% in FY25 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **Tertiary Sector:** Services GVA is estimated to grow by 9.1% in FY26 (9.3% in H1 FY26; 56.4% share in GVA), up from 7.2% in FY25 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).

subject: AGRICULTURE
content_markdown:
PRIMARY SECTOR

• Agriculture
        - **Eco Parameters**
- **Share in GDP:** ~16% of GDP (17.7% of GVA) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **Growth Rate (Recent):** Agricultural growth rebounded from 1.4% in 2023-24 to 3.8% in 2024-25, and registered 3.5% in Q2 FY26 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **Growth Rate (Cumulative):** 4.4% average annual growth over the past 5 years, and 4.45% decadal growth during FY16 to FY25 (highest across decades) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
            - **Agri income:** ↑ 5.23% annually over the past decade.
- **People Employed:** employs ~46.1% of the workforce ([PLFS 2023-24](https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/Press_note_AR_PLFS_2023_24_22092024.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
            - **Agri market:** &rupee;38 lakh crore by 2030.
            - **India is 1st in:** Pulses, Milk
            - **India is 2nd in:** Rice, Wheat, Fruits & Vegetation, arable land.

• Land
        - **Area under Cultivation**
            - 51% of total land area is under cultivation.
            - About 60% of India’s total land area is classified as agricultural land. [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]
        - **Small & Marginal farmers**
            - 89.4% (<2 hectares) [[Economic Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]
            - Cultivate nearly 45% of net sown area ([Agri Census 2015-16](https://agcensus.da.gov.in/)).

• Seed
        - **Saved Seeds** ↠ 85%
        - **Seed Replacement Rate:** 15 – 20%; it’s 100% for hybrid seeds.
        - **Production:** Private firms -> 71% of seed production ([ICAR](https://icar.org.in/))
        - **Role of Seeds:** Impacts 25% of productivity

• Irrigation
        - **Rainfed Agriculture:** 50% of total
        - **Role of Irrigation:** 70% of total input cost
        - **Irrigation coverage:** ↑ from 49.3% to 55% of gross cropped area b/w FY16 and FY21 [[Eco Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]

• Credit
        - **Informal Sector:** around 40%
        - **Debt:** More than 50% farmers under debt
        - **BPL:** 22% of farmers are BPL
        - **Corporate Investment** ↠ < 2%
- **Kisan Credit Card scheme:** 7.72–7.75 crore operational accounts ( ₹10+ lakh crore in KCC credit; total ground-level agricultural credit reached ₹28.67 lakh crore in FY25) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).

• Pesticides
        - 4th largest producer of pesticides
        - **Importance:** 25% crop losses due to pests
        - **Concern:** 0.1% is used of applied reach their intended pest

• Fertilizers [4:2:1]
        - **Consumption:** 655 lakh tonnes fertilizers in FY25
        - **Use vs Productivity:** Fertilizers usage increased 25 times since 1960 but food production increased by only 3 times.
        - **Fiscal Burden:** Fertilizer accounts for large fiscal subsidies
            - &rupee;1.75 lakh crore spent on fertilizer subsidies (2023-24).
            - 2nd highest fiscal expense after food
        - **Imports:** $8.29 billion in 2024-25
        - **Targeting:** Only 35% reach beneficiaries
        - **Urea:**
            - In India, urea is the most produced, imported, consumed and physically regulated fertilizer of all.
            - **Govt spending:** Govt spends &rupee;1,500 per bag of Urea, making it unsustainably cheap for farmers.
            - India is the 2nd largest consumer of urea after China.
        - **DAP:**
            - **Import cost** is $636 (&rupee;55,150) per tonne, while production costs exceed &rupee;65,000 per tonne.
            - **Subsidy Burden:** Govt caps DAP price at &rupee;27,000 per tonne, but the subsidy needed to cover costs is high.

• Storage
        - Short of 30-40 lakh tones ([Ashok Dalwai](https://agricoop.nic.in/en/Doubling))

• Post Harvest Losses
        - 12% of total agricultural GDP
        - 10% of total food grain production ([ICAR](https://icar.org.in/))

• Exports
        - Just 2.4% of world’s share [8th rank]

• Farmer Suicides
        - At least one farmer died by suicide every hour in India [[NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/)]

• Expense in R&D
        - India spends about 0.7% of its agri -GDP on agri -research and Education (R&E)
        - &rupee;1 investment in agri R&D can fetch &rupee;13 return [[Economic Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)].

• Machines
        - Only 40-45% levels of mechanization
        - India ↠ 1/3rd of global tractors

• Crops and Yield
        - Total kharif food grain production -> 1647.05 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) in 2024-25.
        - India's rice yield -> 2,191 kg per hectare (global average 3,026 kg per hectare).
        - Wheat yield -> 2,750 kg/hectare (global avg 3,289 kg/hectare).

• Cotton
        - **Yield:** 435kg/hectare; similar to 2024-25’s yield of 447kg/hectare.
        - **Rainfed crop:** 67% of India’s cotton is produced on rain-fed areas and 33% on irrigated lands
        - **Acreage:** India ranks 1st in cotton acreage with around 40% of the world area under cotton
        - **Production:** India ranks 2nd in cotton production with estimated production of 343.47 lakh bales (5.84 MMT) in 2022-23 i.e. 23.83% of world cotton production.
        - **Productivity:** 39th rank in overall cotton yield -> lower than countries like USA, China, Brazil etc.
        - **Consumption:** 2nd largest consumer of cotton -> 22.24% of world cotton consumption (2023).
        - **Exports:** 30 lakh bales i.e. 6% of world export in 2022-23.

• Oilseeds
        - **Contribution:** India contributes about 5-6% of world production.
        - **Area:** India accounts for 15-20% of global oilseed area
        - **Rainfed:** 76% of oilseed cultivation is rainfed.
        - **National Mission on Edible oils- Targets for 2030-31:**
            - Increase primary oilseed production to 69.7 million tonnes (from 39 million tonnes in 2022-23).
            - Expand oilseed cultivation by an additional 40 lakh hectares by targeting rice and potato fallow lands, promoting intercropping.

• Allied Sector: Fisheries
        - **Production:** India is 2nd largest fish producer
        - **Global:** 8% share in global fish production
            - India ranks 2nd in aquaculture production, leads in shrimp production and 3rd in capture fisheries production.
        - **Inland fisheries:** 75% of total fisheries output.
        - **Growth Rate:** > 10% annually
        - **Contribution:**
            - 1.25 % of India GDP
            - 5% of Agriculture’s GDP ([FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/))

• Allied Sector: Livestock
        - India has the world’s largest livestock population
        - Largest milk producer (23% of global milk production).
        - 2nd in egg production, 5th in meat production ([FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/))
        - **Economic contribution:** 5.50% of India’s Gross Value Added (GVA) in 2022-23.
        - **Employment:** 8.8 % of the population; livelihood for 70% of rural households
        - **Insurance:** Only 15.47% of animals are under insurance cover.
        - **Productivity:** Average annual productivity of cattle in India is 1777 kg/animal/year (world average of 2699 kg/animal/year (2019-20)).
        - **Methane emissions:** Enteric methane emission -> 15.1% total global enteric methane emission.

• Allied Sector: Horticulture
        - **Contribution:** Contributes about 33% to the agriculture GVA
- **Production:** 362.08 million tonnes (Final Est. 2024-25; revised up to 367.72 MT as of Aug 2025, comprising 114.51 MT fruits and 219.67 MT vegetables) -> ~90% of total horticulture production ([DAC&FW](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2248987®=3&lang=1) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
        - India is the 2nd largest producer of fruits and vegetables
        - **Share in Global market Exports:** mere 1%
        - **Exports:** India ranked 14th in vegetables and 23rd in fruits
        - India is the largest producer of Onions, ginger and okra among vegetables and ranks 2nd in production of Potatoes, Cauliflowers, Brinjal, Cabbages, etc ([FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/))

• Organic Farming
        - **No. of farmers:** India ranks 1st in terms of number of farmers -> Home to 30% of total organic producers
        - **Area under Cultivation:** 1.76 million hectares
        - **Certified area:** India ranks at 4th place in terms of certified area globally [International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements]
        - **Sikkim:** 1st State in the world -> fully organic
        - **Lakshadweep** is the only UT declared 100% organic.

• Food Processing
        - India’s FPI is 6th largest in the world.
        - **Contribution:**
            - 7.7% to manufacturing GVA
            - Valued at USD 160 billion
            - 22.6% in agri food exports
        - **Growth Rate:** > 10%
        - 75% of industry is unorganized
        - **FDI:** 100% FDI in food processing under automatic route and 100% FDI in trading, including e-commerce.
        - **Potential:** Indian food processing industry to reach $700 billion by 2030.

• Public Distribution System
        - **NFSA 2013:** Covers 67% of population
            - **Rural Area:** 75%
            - **Urban Area:** 50%
- **Beneficiaries of NFSA (PMGKAY):** 80.56 crore beneficiaries identified out of targeted 81.35 crore (free foodgrains extended for 5 years from Jan 2024 to Dec 2028) ([DFPD](https://dfpd.gov.in/)).
            - 80.56 cr people have been identified, out of the targeted 81.35 cr
        - **Food Subsidy Expense:** 50% of India's total subsidy spending in FY 2024-25
        - **Fair Price Shops:** > 5 Lac shops are there with almost 100% automation.

• Mining
        - **Contribution:** B/w 2.2% and 2.5% of India’s GDP
        - **Employment:** approximately 1.3 million people
        - **Mine closure:** An average of 100 mine workers per day face potential unemployment by 2035 due to mine closure (Global Energy Monitor)

subject: INDIAN ECONOMY
content_markdown:
SECONDARY SECTOR

• Manufacturing
- **Current:** ~17% of GVA (Manufacturing GVA grew by 7.72% in Q1 and 9.13% in Q2 of FY26; Industry GVA grew 7.0% in H1 FY26) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
            - **Potential:** 27% by 2047.
        - **Employment:** 11% [6.5 cr people]
        - **Targets** as per National Manufacturing Policy (NMP), 2011
            - **GDP Share of Manufacturing:** 25% of GDP by 2025
            - **Employment in Manufacturing:** ~10 crore jobs by 2025
        - **India Vs China:** India holds 2.8% of the global manufacturing share, compared to China's 28.8%.

• Industry Sector
        - 27 - 29% of GDP
        - 25% of workforce is employed ([ILO 2023](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/@dgreports/@dcomm/@publ/documents/publication/wcms_711919.pdf))

• MSME
        - 2nd Largest employer after Agriculture
        - 29% to India's GDP [Potential: 40% to GDP by 2030]
        - 40% of Exports
        - Employing 7.5 crore people; 62% to employment in India (McKinsey Global Institute)
        - 95% firms → Unorganised
- **Registered MSMEs:** >5.93 crore registered on Udyam portal ([Ministry of MSME 2025](https://udyamregistration.gov.in/))
        - **MSMEs on e-Commerce Platforms:** Only 6% of MSMEs actively use e- commerce platforms for sales.
        - **PM Mudra Yojana: MSMEs**
- **Accounts:** 55.45 crore loan accounts sanctioned as of October 2025 (up from ~35 crore) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **Credit support:** disbursed over ₹36.18 lakh crore as of October 2025 (up from ₹18.39 lakh crore) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
            - **Women entrepreneurs:** 71.4 % of total no. of accounts (FY 2022).
            - **Categories:** Majority loan accounts (~80%) are in the Shishu category (FY 2021), followed by Kishore at 18.70 %.

• Special Economic Zone (SEZ)
        - India has 280 Operational SEZs (Nov 2024)
        - **Employment:** 2.8 million jobs.
        - **Exports:** $163.69 billion in 2023-24

• Electronics Sector
        - **India’s share in Global Electronics Market:** only 4%
- **Electronics Production:** ₹9.52 lakh crore in FY24 (crossed ₹11.5 lakh crore in FY25; PLI schemes across 14 sectors attracted >₹2.0 lakh crore investment, generating >₹18.7 lakh crore production and >12.6 lakh jobs as of Sep 2025) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
        - **Mobile phones:** India is 2nd largest mobile phone producer in World.
            - 325 million+ mobile phones manufactured in India every year.
            - 99% of smartphones sold in India are now made domestically.
        - **Exports:** Expected to reach $120 Bn by FY26.
        - CAGR of around 25% through 2028.
- **Semiconductor Market:** Projected to grow at 13% reaching ₹8.9 lakh crore by 2030; India Semiconductor Mission approved 10 projects across 6 states worth ₹1.60 lakh crore (ISM 2.0 announced in [Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf) / [Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).

• Pharmaceutical
        - 3rd Largest by volume, 14th Largest by value
        - **Generic Medicines:** India is the largest manufacturer of generic medicines globally.
        - **Economic Contribution:** 1.72% to the GDP [Projected to reach USD 130 billion by 2030]
            - **Market Value:** $50 billion.
        - **Vaccines:** India supplies over 50% of global vaccine demand
        - **Exports:** India ranks 12th globally in medical goods exports
        - **US Imports:** US imports USD 9 billion worth of pharma formulations from India annually.

• Toy Industry
        - **Market value:** 1.5 Billion USD in 2023
            - Projected to increase to $3 billion by 2028
        - **Exports:** USD 326 million to USD 348 million for the last three years.
            - **India's Share:** 0.3% in 2022; **China:** 80%

• Textile Industry
        - **GDP:** 2.3% to India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) [Projected to reach 5% by 2030].
        - **Employs** 4.5 crore workers [After agriculture, textiles and apparel form the second-largest employer in India]
        - **Exports:** 8.21% of India’s total merchandise exports
            - India is the 6th largest exporter of textiles and apparel globally ([Eco Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/))
            - **India’s global trade share:** 4% in textiles and apparel
        - **Capacity:** 2nd largest textile manufacturing capacity globally
        - **FDI:** 100% FDI allowed in textiles under the automatic route.
        - **Fabric Production [India]**
            - Silk → 2nd largest producer
            - Cotton → 2nd largest producer
            - Jute → largest producer
            - Man-Made fibres (MMF) → largest producer

• Sugar Industry
        - **India as Consumer:** Largest in World
        - **India as Producer:** 2nd Largest in World
- **India as Exporter:** 3rd largest in World (typos fixed: 3rd -> 3rd)
        - **India’s Share in Global Sugar Production:** 19%
        - **Employment:** Livelihood for 5 crore farmers and their families.

• Steel Industry
        - **India as Consumer:** 3rd Largest in World after China and USA.
        - **India as Producer:** 2nd Largest in World of crude steel
        - **FDI:** 100% FDI allowed under the automatic route.
        - **Finished steel consumption (Per capita):** 97.7 kgs (2023-24)
        - **Capital-Intensive Sector:** INR 7,000 crore is required to set up 1 tonne of steel- making capacity through the greenfield route.

• Make in India Progress
        - **Toy:** India produces 400 million Toys annually
        - **Mobiles:** India is the second-largest mobile manufacturer in the world
        - **Ease of Doing Business**
            - India climbed from 142nd in 2014 to 63rd in the World Bank's Doing Business Report (DBR), 2020 before its discontinuation.
            - Over 40000 compliances have been reduced and 3,800 provisions decriminalized.

subject: INDIAN ECONOMY
content_markdown:
TERTIARY SECTOR

• Service Sector
- **Economic contribution:** 56.4% of GVA in FY26 FAE (highest ever; 53.6% of GDP in H1 FY26, ~55% of GDP overall) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
            - **Potential:** By 2047, the services sector is expected to contribute 60 per cent of India’s GDP.
        - 30% of the Workforce ([Eco survey 24-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/))
- **Growth Rate:** Estimated at 9.1% in FY26 (9.3% in H1 FY26), after >6% annual growth over the past decade ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
        - **Exports:** India ranked 7th worldwide in global services exports
- **India's share in Global Services Exports:** 4.3% in CY 2024 (more than doubled from 2% in 2005; services exports hit record USD 387.6 billion in FY25 and USD 421.3 billion in FY26) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf) / [MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
            - **IT, Computer services and Business Services Exports:** ~70% of India's services exports.

• IT Sector
- India is 2nd largest Exporter of Software, after USA (typo fixed: 2nd -> 2nd)
        - **Contribution:** 7.5% of India's GDP (as of FY23)
            - Projected to hit 10% by FY25
        - **Outsourcing market:** India is a leading exporter of IT and BPM services, holding about 56% of the global outsourcing market.
        - **Market potential:** Domestic software market is projected to hit $100 billion by 2035 [SaaS Boomi report]

• Tourism
        - 5% of GDP
        - **Employment:** 7.6 crore jobs in FY23 | 7% of Employment
        - **Travel & Tourism Development Index (TTDI) 2024:** 39/119
        - **Inbound visitor markets for India in 2023:** Bangladesh (9%), the United States (9%), and the United Kingdom (6%).

• E-Commerce
        - **Share:** Around 8% of total Retail market [2023-24]
            - up from 4–5% in 2018–19
        - **Growth Rate:** More than 20% [That is a CAGR of 27%]
        - **Potential:** India’s E-commerce market is expected to grow to $325 billion by 2030 [[Invest India](https://www.investindia.gov.in/india-fdi-investment-key-sectors)]

• FinTech
        - India ranks as 3rd largest and fastest-growing fintech market globally.
        - **India’s fintech adoption rate:** 87%
        - Account for 70% of digital payment transactions.
        - **Growth Rate:** More than 30% [That is a CAGR of 30.26%]

• Telecommunication
        - India is the world’s 2nd largest telecommunications market.
- **Telephone Subscriber Base:** 133.06 crore (1,330.58 million) as of March 2026 (up from 120.08 crore in March 2025) [[TRAI Yearly Performance Indicators 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
- **Overall Tele-Density:** 93.26% as of March 2026 (86.76% in late 2025; 84.57% excluding M2M) [[TRAI 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
- **Urban tele-density:** 151.47% as of March 2026 (up from 131.45% in March 2025) [[TRAI 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
- **Rural tele-density:** 60.46% as of March 2026 (up from 59.06% in March 2025) [[TRAI 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
            - Delhi Service area has maximum tele-density of 274.59%
            - Bihar service area has minimum tele-density of 56.90%
        - **FDI:** 4th largest sector in terms of FDI inflows, contributing 6% of total FDI inflow.

subject: INDIAN ECONOMY
content_markdown:
INCLUSIVE GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT

• Inclusive Growth
        - India ranks 62nd out of 74 emerging countries [[Inclusive Development Index, WEF](https://www.weforum.org/)].

• Employment & Unemployment
- **Total Workforce:** 56.2–56.5 crore employed (aged 15+ years in Q2 FY26; over 31 crore unorganised workers registered on e-Shram portal as of Jan 2026, 54% women) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
        - **Need of Jobs:** Indian Economy needs to generate nearly 78.5 lakh jobs annually(non-farm sector) until 2030 to cater need of rising workforce.
- **Unemployment Rate:** 5.1% in monthly PLFS (April 2025); annual usual status (ps+ss) UR stood at 3.2% (female UR at 2.1%) ([MoSPI PLFS Annual Report 2025](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/publications_reports/publications_reports1780040415321_0624fb13-fb47-40bc-b470-7c7e9635c3ef_PLFS_2025_F_REV_29052026.pdf))
        - **Self-Employed Workers:** It has grown from 52.2% in 2017-18 to 58.4% in 2023-24.
        - **Govt Jobs:** 7% of Total employment
        - **Informal Sector:** 90%
        - **Net EPFO Subscriptions:** more than doubling from 61 lakh in FY19 to 131 lakhs in FY24.

• Gig Economy
        - **Total:** Employ over 12 million workers [1.5% of total Workforce]
            - Projected to reach 23.5 million by 2029–30 [[NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf)]
        - **Job creation:** Out of 100 New Jobs, 56 are being created in Gig sector.

• Education & Skills
        - **Stream wise Ratio:**
            - Humanities (33%), Science (15%), Commerce (14%), English (12%)
        - **Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR):** Steady at 23:1 for the last five years.
        - **University Density (per 1 lakh eligible students):** Highest in Sikkim (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (5.6), Ladakh (5.2), etc. In Bihar (0.2), UP (0.3), West Bengal & Maharashtra (0.6) the density is below national average.
        - **Government Spending:**
            - **Expenditure:** 2.9% of GDP
                - Target under NEP 2020: 6% of GDP
- **Budgetary allocation:** ₹1.39 lakh crore (₹1,39,289 crore) allocated to the Ministry of Education in Union Budget 2026-27 (up 8.27% from ₹1.28 lakh crore in 2025-26) ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).
        - **Inefficient Infrastructure [[UDISE+ 2023-24 Report](https://udiseplus.gov.in/)]**
            - **Computers:** The percentage of schools having computers ↑ from 38.5 % in 2019-20 to 57.2 % in 2023-2024.
            - **Internet:** Percentage of schools having internet facility increased from 22.3 % in 2019-20 to 53.9 % in 2023-2024.
            - **Electricity:** Of the over 14.71 lakh schools in India, up to 1.52 lakh schools have no functional electricity.
            - **Drinking Water:** While 14.47 lakh schools claim to have drinking water facilities, only 14.11 lakh have them functional.
            - **Toilets:** Government schools constitute the majority of the 67,000 schools operating without functional toilets.
            - **Differently-Abled Students:** Only 33.2% of government schools have disabled-friendly toilets.
            - **Digital Education:** 46 % schools have functional computers ([Ministry of Education](https://www.education.gov.in/))
        - **Universities and Colleges:**
- **Institutions:** Total Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) increased from 51,534 in 2014-15 to 70,018 as of June 2025 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) [1,168 universities, 45,473 colleges and 12,002 stand-alone institutions in AISHE 2021-22].
            - **Accreditation:** Only 37% of universities are accredited
            - **Growth:** In last 10 years, number of universities has increased by 60%, colleges up 21% [[Ministry of Education](https://www.education.gov.in/)]
            - **Increased Penetration in Rural Areas:** 43% Universities and 61.4% colleges are located in Rural Areas.
            - **Institutes of National Importance (INIs):** 171 [June 2024]
            - **Medical Colleges:** 102% increase-> rising from 387 before 2014 to 780 in 2024
                - **Increase in MBBS seats:** 130% rise in MBBS seats
            - **IIMs:** 21
            - **IITs:** 23
        - **Startup:**
            - **Definition:** An entity, HQ in India, opened less than 10 years ago, and annual turnover < &rupee;100 crore.
- **Recognized startups:** DPIIT-recognized startups increased from ~500 (2016) to over 2.23 lakh as of March 31, 2026 (up from 1.59 lakh in early 2025) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)).
            - **Positive Ecosystem:** 3rd largest startup ecosystem in India
            - **High Failure Rate:** 90% fail within 5 years.
- **Employment Generation:** Recognized startups have created over 23.36 lakh direct jobs as of March 31, 2026 (up from 16.6 lakh in Oct 2024) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2))
- **Women Entrepreneurship:** Over 1.07 lakh recognized startups have at least one woman director/partner as of March 31, 2026 (~48% of [DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)-recognised startups, up from 73,151) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)).
        - **Pain Points:**
            - **Higher Education:**
                - Only 42.6% of Indian graduates are employable [India's Graduate Skill Index 2025]
                - **QS World Rankings 2025: Top Indian Institutes**
                    - No Institute in TOP 100
                    - **IIT Bombay:** Leading in India, IIT Bombay climbed from 149th in 2024 to 118th in 2025.
                    - **IIT Delhi:** Achieved the second position in India, moving up 47 ranks from 197th to 150th.
            - **Schools:**
                - **ASER 2024**
                    - **Reading skill:** 76.6% of Class 3 students still cannot read Class 2 text.
                    - **Foundational Numeracy Skills:** Over 50% of students (14-18 age) face difficulties with elementary division problems.
                    - **Arithmetic:** 66.3% of Class 3 students and 70% of Class 5 students cannot perform simple arithmetic calculations.
                    - Class 3 students able to do subtraction is just 33.7% in 2024.
                - **Vocational Training:** Only about 2% have received formal vocational training [Ministry of Skill Development]
                - **Problem in Basic Skills:**
                    - **NCERT Report 2022:** 11% of Class 3 students in India lack basic skills in Mathematics.

• Skill (General State)
        - **Formally Skilled Workforce:** < 5%
            - South Korea: 95%
            - Japan: 80%
            - Germany: 75%
            - USA: 50%
        - **Employability of Graduates:** Only 51% graduates employable [[Economic Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)]
        - **Vocational Training to Workforce:** 65.3% has received no form of vocational training [[Economic Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)]
        - **Low Formal Training:** only 2.7% of India’s workforce has received formal skill training, compared to 52% in US, 80% in Japan, and 96% in South Korea.

• Deeptech Startup ecosystem
        - **Global Standing:** Despite having the 3rd largest pool of DeepTech startups, India ranked 6th among the top 9 DeepTech ecosystems in the world in 2023 (Nasscom).

• Insurance
        - **Insurance Penetration:** 3.7% of GDP in FY24 [Global average: 7%]
            - Life Insurance penetration: 2.8%
            - Non-Life insurance remained at 1%.
        - India ranks 10th in the global life insurance market.

• Pension Sector
        - **Participation:** Only about 12% of the Indian workforce participates in any formal pension scheme.
        - **NPS & APY Coverage:** Combined National Pension System (NPS) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY) subscribers cover approximately 5.3% of India’s population as of early 2025.

• Poverty
        - **India – Poverty**
            - **Percentage:** 21.9% {2011, Tendulkar Report}
- **Extreme poverty:** Under the World Bank's revised International Poverty Line ($3.00/day at 2021 PPP, up from $2.15/day), India's extreme poverty rate stood at 5.3% in 2022-23 (and 23.9% at the lower-middle-income line) [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]
            - **Decrease in Poverty [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]**
                - **Extreme Poverty Lift:** 171 Million lifted from Extreme Poverty in last decade.
                - **India’s Poverty Rate (at the 3.65 dollars per day line) ->** Fell from 61.8 percent in 2011-12 to 28.1 percent in 2022-23.
                    - Rural poverty declined from 69 percent to 32.5 percent
                    - Urban poverty dropped from 43.5 percent to 17.2 percent.
- **Non-monetary poverty (Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)) ->** declined from 55.3% in 2005-06 to 11.28% in 2022-23 ([NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) [[UNDP](https://hdr.undp.org/) MPI: 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21].
        - **Global – Poverty**
            - **Incidence:** 8.5% of total population i.e. 75 cr live in extreme poverty - on less than $2.15 per day [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]
            - **Deprived Regions:** 5 out of 6 poor are in Sub-Saharan or South Asia
            - **Rural > Urban –** over 75% of all poor live in rural areas.
            - **High Prevalence among Children (< 18):** 50% of total poor
        - **Global Inequality ([Oxfam](https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/takers-not-makers-unjust-poverty-and-unearned-wealth-colonialism)):**
            - The richest 1% control 45% of global wealth.
            - 44% of the world's population lives below the World Bank's poverty line of $6.85 (PPP).
        - **India Inequality ([Oxfam](https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/takers-not-makers-unjust-poverty-and-unearned-wealth-colonialism)):**
            - Richest 1% control more than 40% of total wealth
            - Bottom 50% own merely 3% 3. Gini Index
        - **Gini Coefficient:**
            - The Gini coefficient improved for rural areas (declined to 0.237 in 2023-24 from 0.266 in 2022-23) and urban areas (declined to 0.284 in 2023-24 from 0.314 in 2022-23).

• Hunger
        - **Status of Hunger [[Global Hunger Index 2024](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]**
            - **Global:**
                - 2.8 billion people cannot afford a healthy diet.
            - **India Specific:**
- **India's Rank:** Improved to 102nd out of 123 countries in Global Hunger Index 2025 (up from 105th out of 127 in GHI 2024; remains in the "serious" category) [[GHI 2025](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]
                - **Child Wasting Rate:** 18.7% [Highest in World]
- **Stunted Children:** 32.9% in GHI 2025 (down from >35% earlier;Child Wasting remains 18.7%) [[GHI 2025](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]
                - **Under-5 mortality:** 2.9%
        - **Status of Food Security [[State of Food Security and Nutrition Report (2024)](https://www.fao.org/publications/home/fao-flagship-publications/the-state-of-food-security-and-nutrition-in-the-world)]**
            - **India Specific:**
                - **Undernourished:** 13% from Chronic Undernourishment
                - **Anemic:** 53% of Women
        - **UN-FAO Report:**
            - Hunger in India came down to 13.7% during 2021-23 period

• Regional Disparity
        - **Delhi’s per capita Income** = 2.5 times of national average [[EAC-PM](https://eacpm.gov.in/)]
        - **Rural-Urban Inequality [[Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports)]**
            - **Rural Area:** &rupee;4,122 MPCE
            - **Urban Area:** &rupee;6,996 MPCE [Higher by around 70%]
        - **OoPE (Health):**
            - **Decrease in OoPE:** OOPE as a percentage of total health expenditure (THE) declined from 62.6% in 2014-15 to 39.4% in 2021-22 [[National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates](https://nhsrcindia.org/national-health-accounts-records)]
            - **People Pushed into Poverty:** 6 crore people pushed into poverty every year, due to OoPE [[NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf)]

• DIVERSITY
        - **Caste System:**
            - **Jatis:** More than 30000 Jatis
            - **Inter-faith and Intercaste marriages:** around 6%
                - 61% of respondents opposed interfaith marriages; 56% were against inter-caste unions [India Today's Gross Domestic Behaviour survey]
                - **Rural Vs Urban:** Inter-caste marriages are more frequent in Rural areas (5.2%) than Urban areas (4.9%) [Indian Statistical Institute study]
                - **Rich and poor:** Inter-caste marriages are more common among poor people (5.9%) than rich people (4.0%).
        - **Diversity:**
            - **Tribes:** 705
            - **Languages:** 121 (> 10 K) | 1500 spoken
            - **Dialects:** 20,000 languages or dialects.
            - **Hindi Speakers:** only 26% speak Hindi as mother tongue
        - **Communalism:**
            - **No. of Communal Riots:** India witnessed 84% rise in communal violence in 2024 [Centre for Study of Society and Secularism (CSSS) report]
            - **States:**
                - Maharashtra emerged → 12 riots.
                - Uttar Pradesh and Bihar → 7 riots

BANKING & MONEY MARKET

• Banking - NPA
- **Gross NPAs:** Multi-decadal low of 2.2% in September 2025 (and Net NPA at record low of 0.5%), down from 2.6% in September 2024 [[RBI](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63744) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]
        - **Bad Loans:** Banks have written off NPAs worth about Rs 16.35 trillion in last 10 financial years
        - **Credit card NPAs** spiked 500% in past four years [[RBI data](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/FSReports.aspx)]

• Banks
- **Bank Accounts (PMJDY):** increased from 14.72 Cr in March 2015 to 55.02 Cr as of March 2025 (with 36.63 Cr in rural/semi-urban areas and ~56% owned by women) [[Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)].
        - **Credit-Deposit Ratio ([RBI’s Financial Stability Report](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/FSReports.aspx)):**
            - CD ratio has been rising since September 2021 and peaked at 78.8% in December 2023.
            - Over 75% of banks with CD ratios > 75% are private sector banks.
- **Capital-to-risk-weighted assets ratio (CRAR)** for SCBs stands at ~16.7–17.2% in FY25/FY26, well above the 11.5% regulatory norm ([RBI FSR](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/FSReports.aspx) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
        - **Profits:**
            - Public sector banks record cumulative net profit of Rs 1.78 lakh crore for FY25.
            - All 12 PSBs reported profits, marking a significant turnaround from losses in FY18.
            - HDFC Bank remains the most profitable private bank in India, with a net profit of Rs 73,440 crore in FY25.

• Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)
        - 92% branches in Rural/Semi-Urban areas
        - Around 90% of loans goes to Priority sector lending, with around 70% of loans to the Agriculture Sector.

subject: INDIAN ECONOMY
content_markdown:
NATIONAL INCOME & ACCOUNTING

• GDP
- **GDP Estimates (FY25 Provisional & FY26 First Advance Estimates - [MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1767781372753_1380ce82-f5a5-440d-99e6-e6b35af0deb5_GDP_Press_Note_on_FAE_2025-26.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)):**
- Real GDP grew by 7.4% in FY26 (FAE) after 6.5% growth in FY25 (₹187.97 lakh crore) ([MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1767781372753_1380ce82-f5a5-440d-99e6-e6b35af0deb5_GDP_Press_Note_on_FAE_2025-26.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
            - Nominal GDP rose by 9.8% to ₹330.68 lakh crore.

• Inflation
- **India's Retail Inflation (CPI):** Dropped sharply to a series-low average of 1.7% in FY26 (April–December 2025), down from 4.9% in Apr–Dec 2024 and 5.4% in FY24 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
        - **Projections:** IMF has projected an inflation rate of 4.4% in FY25 and 4.1% in FY26 for India.
        - **Food inflation** increased from 7.5 % in FY24 to 8.4 % in FY25 (April - December).
        - **Headline Inflation:** RBI expects headline inflation to be 4.2% in FY26, if there is normal monsoon and no further external or policy shocks.

• Savings Rate
        - **India Gross Savings Rate:** 30.7% in Mar 2024
        - **Household Financial Savings** to reach 6.5% of Gross national disposable income (GNDI) in FY25 [[SBI report](https://sbi.co.in/web/corporate-governance/ecowrap)]

• Fiscal Policy & Government Budget
        - **Debt Profile**
            - **Government Debt to GDP** (Centre and states) - **around 83.1%** (by 2024 end)
- **Central Government [Debt to GDP]** – Estimated at 56.1% in RE 2025-26 and 55.6% in BE 2026-27 (down from 57.1% in 2024-25) ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455))
                - Government aims to bring it down to 50 ± 1% by 2030–31
            - **State Government [Debt to GDP]** – 26%
            - **Debt of the Central Government:**
                - **Internal debt:** 94%
                - **Public Debt:** 89.9%
                - **External Debt:** 6%
            - **External Debt to GDP Ratio:** In India, external debt constituted 19.4% of the total GDP at the end of September 2024.
                - Across currencies, the external debt remained primarily denominated in the US Dollar (53.4 %), followed by the INR (31.2 %), SDR (5 %), and the Euro (3 %).

• Foreign Trade
- **India's Total Exports:** Scaled an all-time high of **$863.1 billion in FY 2025-26** ($441.8B merchandise + $421.3B services), up from $825.3 billion in FY 2024-25 ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
            - **Exports in 2016:** It was around USD 435 billion in FY 2016.
            - **India’s target** for export is USD 2 Trillion by 2030.
        - **Trade**
            - **Deficit:** Overall trade deficit -> USD 78.1 billion in FY24 ([Eco Survey 2023-24](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2024-25/economicsurvey/index.php)).
- **Largest Trade Deficit:** China [$112.6 billion in FY 2025-26, up from $99.2 billion in FY 2024-25] ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
- **Largest Trading Partner:** China surpassed the USA in FY 2025-26 (in FY 2024-25, USA was 1st with $131.84 billion bilateral trade and $40.89B surplus; in FY26, India-US trade surplus was $34.4B) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
            - **India’s Top Export Destinations:** USA (17.90%) > UAE (8.23%) > Netherlands (5.16%) > China (3.85%) > Singapore (3.33%).
            - **India’s Top Import Source Nations:** China > UAE > USA > Russia.
        - **Remittances:**
            - India is the **largest recipient** of remittances globally
- **Remittances Received:** Record **$135.4 billion in FY25** ($129.4 billion in CY 2024) ([RBI](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63744) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
            - The U.S. accounts for 27.7% of India's inward remittances

• Current Account Deficit (CAD)
- **CAD:** Moderated to 0.8% of GDP in H1 FY26 (from 1.3% in H1 FY25; ~1.3% in Q2 FY26) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))

• Forex Reserves
- **US $701.4 billion** as of 16 January 2026 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) and **US $734.6 billion** as of 2 October 2026 ([RBI](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63744)), providing ~11 months of import cover and 94.4% external debt cover.
        - **Import Cover:** It is sufficient to provide an import cover of more than 11 months.

• Investment

• FDI
- **Total FDI inflows** -> $81.04 billion in FY 2024-25 ($64.7 billion in Apr–Nov 2025; total FDI inflows touched $94.53 billion / equity $58.85 billion in FY 2025-26) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
        - India's FDI inflows have increased ~20 times from 2000-01 to 2023-24.
        - **Highest FDI Inflow:** Computer software and hardware.
        - **FDI Source:** Mauritius(25%) > Singapore (23%) > USA (9%)
        - **FDI Top Destinations [FY 2024–25]:** Maharashtra (39%) > Karnataka (13%) > Delhi (12%)

• FPI
        - **FPI Outflows:** FPIs have pulled out a massive &rupee;1.16 lakh crore from Indian equities so far in 2025.

content_markdown:
INFRASTRUCTURE

• Logistics Sector
        - **Logistics Performance Index (LPI 2023):** 38/139
        - **GDP Contribution:** 13-14% to the GDP (NCAER, 2021-22).
        - **Impact on Trade:** Improved logistics can boost trade by 15% in developing economies.
        - **Impact on Exports:** 10% decrease in logistics cost can increase 5-8% of exports.
        - **Carbon Emissions:** India's logistics sector emits 13.5% of nation's GH gases, with road transport—mainly trucks—driving 88% of emissions.

• Modes of Logistic Movement
        - **Modes of Logistic Movement [Both Freight & Passengers]**:
ModeShare
Roads65% share
Rail31% share
Waterways3% share
Air1% share


• Pain Points in Logistics
        - **India's Logistics Cost:** 14–18% of GDP (Global: 8%)
            - **Logistics Cost Reduction:** Declined by 0.8-0.9 percentage points of GDP between FY14-FY22
        - **Unorganized:** Only 5.5–6% of logistics market was held by organised, tech-driven players (EY).
        - **Freight Cost Comparison ([NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf)):**
            - Jamshedpur to Mumbai -> USD 50/tonne
            - Rotterdam to Mumbai-> USD 34/tonne

• Infrastructure - General
- **Current Investment:** Public capital expenditure increased to **₹12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026-27 BE** (up from ₹11.21 lakh crore in FY 2025-26 BE; effective capex ₹15.48 lakh crore in FY26 BE) ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
        - **Investment Required:** India will need to spend around ₹143 trillion by 2030 on infrastructure.
        - **National Infrastructure Pipeline:** The projected infrastructure investment is ₹111 trillion for 2021-25 (over 5 yrs).
        - **Status of NIP [As of March 2025]:**
            - Planned investments rose from ₹111 trillion to ₹168.93 trillion.
            - Completed investments are ₹31.1 trillion, achieving 28% of original target.

• Transport Sector
        - **Contribution to GDP:** ≈ 5%
        - **Share by Different Mode**:
SHARE of Transport TypesCost per tonne/km
Road66% (WB) | Rs 2.5
Rail31% | Rs 1.3

Inland waterways0.15%
Coastal Shipping7%


• Road
        - 2nd largest road network in the world (after the USA).
        - 87% of passengers and 60% of freight traffic annually.
        - **Road density:** 1,926.02 (2018-19)
        - **Length of various categories of roads:**
- National Highways: **1,46,572 km** as of March 2026 (up from 91,287 km in FY14 and 1,46,145 km in 2024; total road network 63.73 lakh km) ([MoRTH](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526))
            - State Highways: 1,86,908 km;
            - Other Roads: 59,02,539 km
        - **National Highway:** 2% of total road network, 40% of total traffic; 5853 km of NH was constructed in FY25..
            - **Expansion:** 65, 569 km in 2004 to 1,46,145 kms in 2024.
        - **Road Accidents:** 172000 lives in 2023 - averaging 474 deaths daily, or one every three minutes.
            - India loses 3% of GDP in road accidents annually (UN Report)
        - **FDI:** 100% FDI in roads and highways is allowed under automatic route.
        - **Bharatmala Pariyojana ->** aims to develop 34,800 km of National Highways.
        - **National High-Speed Corridors (HSCs):** Length of HSCs expanded from 93 km in 2014 to 2,474 km in 2024.
        - **Multi-Modal Logistics Parks (MMLP):** Till December 2024, Six MMLPs in Chennai, Indore, Nagpur, Jalna, Jogighopa and Bangalore have been awarded.

• Railway
- 4th largest network in the world - **69,439 route km** as of March 2025 (with 99.6% rail electrification achieved by July 2026) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526))
        - **Freight:**
            - **In Freight traffic:** 12 times more efficient than roadways
            - **Target freight share:** From current 35% to 45% by 2030 (India’s NDCs).
            - **Average Freight Speed:** 23.6km/h (*USA: 50 km/h)
        - **Over Utilisation:** 150% above capacity
        - **Railway Penetration:** 0.057 km per 1000 persons (USA 0.752 per 1000 persons)
        - **Railway Safety:**
            - 200 major railway accidents in the past five years, 351 people killed.
            - 75% of derailments due to `railway staff failure'
            - 10 % derailments are caused by `equipment failures'.
        - **Passengers:** 715 crore passengers travelled by the Indian Railways between April 1, 2024 and March 31, 2025.
        - **Net zero targets:** Indian Railways targets net zero emissions with 30 GW of renewable energy by 2029-30.
- **Vande Bharat trains:** **162 Vande Bharat train services** (plus 2 Vande Bharat Sleeper and 72 Amrit Bharat services) operational as of July 2026 (up from 136) ([Ministry of Railways](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).
- **Kavach:** Automated Train Protection system (Kavach Version 4.0) commissioned on **2,633 route km** as of July 2026 (₹1,547 crore invested till Nov 2024) ([Ministry of Railways](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).

• Airways
        - **Market size:** 3rd largest in the world, behind the US and China. (Trade Promotion Council of India)
        - **Domestic Passenger traffic:** 165.7 million; 8th biggest passenger traffic.
        - **Airport's cargo handling capacity:** 8.0 million MT in FY24 ([Eco survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
        - **Airline capacity:** doubled from 7.9 million seats in April 2014 to 15.5 million in April 2024.
- **Operational Airports:** **165 operational airports** as of July 2026 (164 in 2025, up from 74 in 2014) ([MoCA](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).
        - **CAGR:** 14.5% in no. of domestic passengers during FY14 and FY20
        - **Profit making Airports:** Only 22 out of 148 operational airports making profit (Parliamentary committee). The Kolkata airport was the most profitable, followed by the Chennai airport.
- **UDAN scheme:** **679 routes connecting 95 airports**, heliports, and water aerodromes operationalised, benefiting >1.68 crore passengers as of July 2026 (Modified UDAN approved in March 2026 with ₹28,840 crore outlay for FY27–FY36) ([MoCA](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).
        - **Women pilots:** 15% women pilots (almost 3 times the global average)

• Waterway
        - **Coastline:** 7516.6 km; Navigable Inland Waterways - 14,500 kms
            - In December 2024, the Union Home Ministry revised India’s coastline length from 7,516.6 km to 11,098.8 km, citing ongoing review due to the coastline paradox. [Read about coastline paradox]
        - **Major ports:** 13, Non-major ports: 200+
        - **Trade through marine transport:** By Volume: 95%; by Value: 70%
        - **Ships (ownership):**
            - 90% are Foreign owned ships
            - 10(departure)
            - 2.73 days (behind Global average)
        - **Average Fleet age:** > 19 years
        - **Inland Waterways:** 2% (China 10%, Bangladesh 32%); **Coastal Shipping:** 6%
- **Average turnaround time for Indian ports** improved from 94 hours (~3.9 days in 2014) to **48.8 hours (~2.03 days) in 2025-26**, with major ports' cargo capacity reaching 1,728 MMTPA and handling 915.17 MT in FY26 ([MoPSW](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).

• Power
        - 3rd largest producer and consumer of electricity worldwide.
- **Installed power capacity:** **509.74 GW as of November 2025** (up 11.6% YoY from 466.24 GW in Jan 2025; total non-fossil installed capacity reached **283.46 GW** as of 31 March 2026, crossing 50% share) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf) / [MNRE](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
        - **Installed Capacity:**
            - Fossil Fuel Based Thermal Power: 248.62 GW
            - Non Fossil Fuel Based Renewable Energy Sources: 217.62 GW
- **Power AT&C / T&D Losses:** AT&C losses reduced from 22.62% (FY14) to **15.04% in FY25**, with DISCOMs recording a positive PAT of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 for the first time ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).

• Digital Economy
        - **Household Digital Literacy:** < 38% [NASSCOM]
            - Urban Areas: 61%
            - Rural Areas: 25%
        - **Individual Digital Literacy:** Only 26.8% of Indian youth in the academic age group have internet browsing skills ([NSO survey](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports))
        - **Digital consumers:** 3rd largest in world after China and USA
- **Internet Subscribers:** **109.28 crore (1,092.79 million)** as of March 2026 (including 106.59 crore broadband subscribers), up from 96.91 crore in March 2025 [[TRAI Yearly Performance Indicators 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)].
            - Rural Internet Penetration: ~53% of rural population
            - Urban Internet Penetration: ~77% of urban population
        - **Digital Payment:** GDP = 86% (100 billion $)

OTHERS

        - **India:**
            - **Market value:** $45 billion by 2030.

• Creative Economy [Orange Economy]

        - **Eco contribution:** 20% contribution by creative occupation to nation overall GVA.
        - **Employment:** Young people (15–29) make up 23% of creative industry jobs—highest across sectors; women hold 45% of creative roles globally.
        - **Exports:** 1.5 times increase in export of creative goods from 2010 to 2019.
        - **Urban areas:** A sizeable 67.07% of all creative workers in India are in the urban areas.

• Gas Based Economy
        - **Aim:** PM aims to raise India's natural gas share from 6.2% to 15% by 2030 (World Avg: 24.42%)
        - **Import dependence:** around 50% of our requirement of Natural gas.
        - **Import bill:** $15.2 billion in FY25.
        - **Importance:** A 10% replacement of liquid fuel into gas will reduce import bill by nearly $3 billion every year.
        - **CNG stations and PNG Connections:** On Dec 2024, India has 7,395 CNG stations and around ~1.47 crore PNG domestic connections.

• SDGs
- **UN Sustainable Development Report 2026:** India achieved its highest-ever rank of **94th out of 167 countries** (score 68.3), improving from 99th in SDR 2025 and 109th in SDR 2024 [[UN SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026](https://dashboards.sdgindex.org/profiles/india/)]
        - **SDG India Index (2023-24):**
            - Composite score improved from 57 in 2018 to 66 in 2020-21 to further to 71 in 2023-24
            - Advancements in Goals 1 (No Poverty), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), 13 (Climate Action).

• Critical Minerals
        - **Global:**
            - **Top Producers:** China > Congo > Chile > Indonesia > South Africa
            - **China Dominance:** China controls 60% of rare earth production, 60% of critical minerals production & 80% of processing worldwide.
        - **India:**
            - **List:** Released list of 30 critical minerals including Bismuth, Cobalt, Copper, Phosphorous, Potash, Rare Earth Elements (REE) etc.
            - **Vulnerability:** 54% of critical materials lie near indigenous people’s land. (International Renewable Energy Agency ([IRENA](https://www.irena.org/)))
            - **Current update:** Presence of 5.9 million tonnes of lithium in J&K.

• Stock Market

- **Indian Investors in Capital Markets:** Unique investors crossed the **12-crore mark in September 2025** (~25% women), total demat accounts crossed **21.6 crore** (Dec 2025), and mutual fund unique investors reached **5.9 crore** [[Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)].

        - **Size of the Indian Bond Market:** US$2.69 trillion [Dec 2024]
        - **Government Securities Market:** $1.3 trillion

content_markdown:
CLIMATE CHANGE

Temperature Rise
- Planet already warmed at least 1.1 degrees Celsius
- 77% of climate experts expect temperature rise > 2.5° by 2100

Rising sea levels
- Risen by over 10 cm between 1993 and 2024 ([NASA](https://climate.nasa.gov/))
- **Projection:** Global mean SLR of 1.3-1.6 m by 2100 in high-emission scenario ([IPCC](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/)).

Carbon emissions
- **Global average CO2 emissions->** 419.3 parts per million in 2023.
- **India (per capita):** 1.9 ton v/s 4.7 ton (World avg)
- **World 3rd largest emitter** (after China, USA)

Greenhouse Gas Emissions [UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2024 & 2025]
- **Ranking:** India ranks 3rd in total GHG emissions (4,140 MtCO2e) [China (1st) & US (2nd)].
- **Meeting climate ambition:** To limit global warming to 1.5°C (UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 'Off Target' puts cuts needed from 2019 levels at 55% by 2035 for 1.5°C and 35% by 2035 for 2°C; EGR 2024 cited 42% by 2030 and 57% by 2035):
    - Nations must cut 42 % off annual GHG emissions by 2030 and
    - 57 % by 2035 in the next NDCs.
5. Warmest year on record: 2024 ([NOAA](https://www.noaa.gov/))
6. Degradation and Desertification: 32% of land affected by degradation and 25%
by desertification

Impacts of climate change

• Ocean Ecosystem
        - Coral reefs decline 70-90% if warming above 1.5°C [[IPCC](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/)]
        - Antarctica losing ice mass at an average rate of about 150 billion tons per year
        - Greenland losing 270 billion tons per year, adding to sea level rise

• Economic losses
        - Decline in labour productivity of up to 40%.
        - 3.8% of total working hours could be lost by 2030 [[World Economic Forum](https://www.weforum.org/)]

• Agriculture
        - ↓ kharif maize yields by 18 and 23% in 2050 and 2080 scenarios, respectively.
        - For every degree of warming, 10-25% increase in crops lost to insect attacks.
        - Exploitable fish biomass show ↓ >10% by mid-century for many regions of world [[FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/)]

• Women
        - 158 million more women and girls into poverty by 2050; 236 million more women into hunger [[UN Women](https://www.unwomen.org/)]

• Extreme events
        - Heatwave made 45 times more likely due to climate change
        - 14.83 crore people in India will be living in severe climate hotspots by 2050 (Council on Energy, Environment and water)
        - > 80% of Indian population lives in districts highly vulnerable to extreme weather events.

• Displacement
        - India may face a migration of 45 million people by 2050.
        - 600 million people could face food insecurity due to climate change- induced disruptions to agriculture and fisheries.
        - Tuvalu expected to be one of the first countries to be completely lost to climate change.

Carbon Inequality
- Richest 1% responsible for more carbon emissions than the poorest 66%.
- Half of all emissions are due to **1/10th** of the global population

IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report
- > 50% chance that global temperature rise will reach or surpass 1.5 degrees Celsius between 2021 and 2040.
- Per-capita GDP in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and West Asia remain lower than global average by 2050 [[IPCC 6th synthesis report](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/)]

Climate finance

• Global
    - **Global climate finance needs** are projected to exceed $10 trillion annually by 2050 ([CAG](https://cag.gov.in/)).
    - **Advanced economies** contributed 45% of climate finance, while **least** **developed countries (LDCs)** received only 3% - From 2018 to 2022 (GLCF 2024).
    - **Adaptation funding gap:** Developing countries need $215–387 billion annually, but receive just $28 billion in 2022 ([Adaptation Gap Report 2024](https://www.unep.org/resources/adaptation-gap-report-2024)).
    - **Mitigation-adaptation imbalance**-> 90% of climate finance directed toward mitigation ([UNDP](https://hdr.undp.org/)).
    - **Funding source:** > 94% of current climate investment comes through debt or equity, rather than grants (Climate Policy Initiative).

• India's Climate Finance Needs
        - India estimates a $2.5 trillion financing need by 2030 for its climate transition to achieve net-zero emissions by 2070.
        - 6–8 trillion USD needed during 2015–2030 to transform current energy systems in India.
        - **Adaptation spending:** ↑ from 3.7% of GDP in FY16 to 5.6% in FY22 ([Eco Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))

• Quantified Goal on Climate Finance (NCQG) or Baku Finance Goal
        - Triple finance to USD 300 billion annually by 2035 (previous goal of USD 100 billion annually).
        - Secure efforts to mobilize $1.3 trillion per year by 2035 from both public and private sources
    - **COP29**-> proposed climate finance goal of USD 300 billion annually by 2035 is much lower than the estimated USD 5.1-6.8 trillion needed by 2030 ([Eco Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
11. LiFE: By 2030, LiFE could save consumers USD 440 billion globally.
12. Paris agreement status: Current pledges put world on track for a 2.5-2.9°C
temperature rise– far above the 1.5°C limit [[UNEP Emission Gap report](https://www.uncclearn.org/wp-content/uploads/library/EGR2025.pdf)]

India's Climate Commitments
- Panchamrit (COP-26)
        - Non-fossil fuel energy capacity to 500 gigawatts (GW) by 2030;
        - 50% of its energy needs from renewable sources by 2030;
        - ↓ carbon emissions by 1 billion tonnes from the present until 2030;
        - Reduce emissions intensity of its GDP by 45% by 2030.
        - Net Zero emissions by 2070.
14. India’s demands: India wants to push developed nations to become carbon
negative rather than carbon neutral by 2050. ### Section Group: Conservation & Ecosystems

content_markdown:
BIODIVERSITY

Protected areas
- 1014 Protected areas-> covers 1,75,169.42 km2 of geographical area -> ≈ 5.32%.
- 72% rise in the number and 16% growth in the total area from 2000 to 2023.
- Bid to double global protected areas affect India’s tribes
    - 84% of national parks are established in areas inhabited by STs.

Biodiversity hotspots
- India lost 90% of area under its four biodiversity hotspots (CSE Data, 2021)
- 25 species have gone extinct in these hotspots.
- **Global:** 36 biodiversity hotspots
    - Represent just 2.5% of Earth's land surface
    - Supports > half of the world's plant species as endemics
    - Supports 43% of bird, mammal, reptile and amphibian species as endemics.

Illegal wildlife trade
- 4th most illegal trade after arms, drugs and human trafficking.
- Annual value -> $7 - $23 billion (2016 UN estimates)
- Rhino horn (29%), followed by pangolin scales (28%) and elephant ivory (15%) [[World Wildlife Crime report, 2024](https://www.unodc.org/cofrb/uploads/documents/ECOS/World_Wildlife_Crime_Report_2024.pdf)]
4. Illegally traded plants: Cedars mahogany, holy wood, and Guiacum made up
biggest market at 47%.

Human wildlife conflict
- **Elephant deaths:** 94 elephants perished due to electrocution in 2023-24
- **Tiger deaths:** > 600 people were killed in tiger attacks in the country between 2014 and 2024, an average of 60 deaths annually
- **Agriculture loss:** Wild herbivores damage 15-50% of standing crops in field
- **Poaching:** > 6,900 poachers were arrested for killing and trafficking of 2,869 wildlife animals during the past 10 years
- India is among the top three countries globally for illegal wildlife trade via the airline sector.

Invasive species
- India
        - India tops the list with 185 invasive alien plants in South Asia.
        - 66% of country's natural systems threatened
        - Economic cost could reach up to USD 182.6 billion.
- Global
        - 37,000 established alien species
        - 1 in 10 species on IUCN Red List are threatened by invasive alien species.
        - Annual economic costs exceed USD 423 billion.

Coastal areas
- 33.6% of Indian coastline vulnerable to erosion, 26.9% was under accretion (growing) and 39.6% was in stable state.

Forests
- India State of Forest Report (2023)
        - **Forest and Tree cover:** 25.17 percent of the geographical area and (21.76% is forest cover and 3.41% is tree cover).
            - ↑ by 1,445.81 km², with a 156.41 km² rise in forest cover compared to 2021.
        - **State-wise data**
            - **Area wise** top three states having largest forest cover are Madhya Pradesh > Arunachal Pradesh > Chhattisgarh
            - **Maximum increase (Forest and Tree Cover):** Chhattisgarh > Uttar Pradesh > Odisha > Rajasthan
            - **Largest Decrease:** MP > Karnataka > Ladakh > Nagaland
            - 19 states/UTs have above 33 percent of the geographical area under forest cover.
        - **Mangrove cover**: 4,992 sq km - 0.15% of the total geographical area, with a net decrease of 7.43 km² since 2021.
        - **Carbon stock:** 30.43 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent.

Mangroves
- **Total mangrove cover:** 4,992 sq km ([ISFR 2023](https://fsi.nic.in/uploads/isfr2023/isfr_book_eng-vol-1_2023.pdf))
- **Vulnerability**: By 2070, 50% of India’s mangroves will shift or vanish due to climate change [Birbal Sahni institute Palaeosciences]
- **Global:** Over 50% of world’s mangroves at risk of collapse, climate change leading factor; ([IUCN](https://www.iucn.org/)).

Coral reefs
- Global
        - Cover less than 1% of ocean floor but most productive and diverse ecosystem.
        - **Bleaching:** > 60% of world's coral reefs may have bleached in past year ([NOAA](https://www.noaa.gov/))
        - **Effect of Climate change:** It **c**ould damage half of the world's reefs by 2035
        - NOAA confirms 4th global coral bleaching event
- India
        - **Bleaching:** 84.6% of coral reefs in Lakshadweep experienced bleaching during 2023-24 [Ministry of Earth Sciences informed (MoES)]
        - It takes 6-7 years for Lakshadweep reefs to recover, without further disturbances
        - Degradation can affect 4.5 million people in southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean.

Wetlands
- 4.6% of land as wetlands; 15.26 million hectares
- India now has **101 Ramsar sites** (covering 13.88 lakh hectares across 28 states/UTs as of August 2026, up from 89 sites earlier; highest in Asia) ([MoEFCC](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100) / [Ramsar Convention 2026](https://indianwetlands.in/wp-content/uploads/library/1761126102.pdf))
- **National Wetland Atlas (2011):** Gujarat (17.5%), lowest in Mizoram (0.66%)
- India lost 2 out of 5 wetlands in last 3 decades
- Global
        - 35% of the world's wetlands lost b/w 1970-2015
        - 30% of coastal wetlands could be lost by 2100

Beaches
- **18 Blue Flag Certified beaches** in India across 7 coastal states and 2 UTs as of the 2025-26 season (up from 12) ([MoEFCC Year-End Review 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100))
- 89% of shoreline of A&N islands eroded by Bay of Bengal
- 33.6% of Indian coastline was vulnerable to erosion

Species
- **Extinct species:** Indian Cheetah, pink-headed duck, and the Great Indian Bustard due to desertification.

• Tiger
        - ↑ by 30% in the last 20 years.
- 3,682 tigers (range 3,167–3,925, accounting for ~75% of global wild tiger population) ([NTCA All India Tiger Estimation 2022/2023](https://ntca.gov.in/tiger-reserves/))
        - 53.2% of tiger deaths occurred within Tiger Reserves
        - 35.22% happened outside boundary of TRs ([NTCA](https://ntca.gov.in/tiger-reserves/))
        - Tiger deaths in 2023 is highest (178) since 2012.

• Elephants
        - India has the largest number of wild Asian Elephants
        - Decline in India's Elephant Population-> From 19.8K in 2017 to 15.9K in 2023 ([WII](https://wii.gov.in/))
        - 29,964 elephants (2017 census by Project Elephant).
        - 60% of the species’ global population in India.

• Birds Population
        - **State of India’s Birds (2023)**
            - 60% of bird species declined in India over a period of 30 years
            - 29% are stable, and 11% have shown increases.
        - **Global**
            - 48% of 11,000 surviving bird species experiencing decline
            - 13.5% of bird species face risk of global extinction, with 798 species classified as vulnerable, 460 as endangered, and 223 as critically endangered.
14. Ecosystem services: Total value of global ecosystem services for one year is b/w
16 to 54 trillion USD

content_markdown:
ENERGY - RENEWABLE & NON-RENEWABLE
India’s Energy Mix (Sources and Shares) [ As per [Energy Statistics India 2025](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports) ,
[MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1767781372753_1380ce82-f5a5-440d-99e6-e6b35af0deb5_GDP_Press_Note_on_FAE_2025-26.pdf)]
- Coal: 48%
- Oil: 28%
- Natural Gas: 8%
- Renewables (Solar, Wind, Hydro, Biomass): 12%
- Nuclear: 4%

Non-renewable energy

• Coal energy
    - Coal-> 46.88% of India's total installed capacity for power generation.
    - Share in total power generation capacity ↓ below 50% in 2024 (first time since 1960s).
    - **Coal Imports** decreased by 8.4% in April-December 2024 in comparison to the same period of FY 2023-24.
    - **Per capita commercial primary energy consumption:** 350 kgoe/year.
    - 5th largest geological reserves of coal
- Future of Coal
        - **Expected demand:** 1.3-1.5 billion tonnes by 2030 ([Eco Survey 2022- 23](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2023-24/economicsurvey/index.php))

• Natural gas
    - Share in energy basket-> 8% (Target: 15% by 2030).
    - **Consumption:** 164.3 million metric standard cubic meters per day (mmscmd).
    - CNG vehicle sales jump 38% in FY2024
    - India emerges as key market for LNG, ranks fourth globally in 2024

• Nuclear energy
    - 5th largest source of electricity
    - 4% of the total electricity generation
    - 25 operable nuclear energy reactors with a total installed capacity of 8.88 GW
    - **Target:** 1 lakh MW by 2047

Renewable energy

• Solar energy
    - **Potential:** 748 GWp (National Institute of Solar Energy)
- **Installed capacity:** **150.26 GW as of 31 March 2026** (including 110.43 GW utility-scale, 25.73 GW rooftop solar, and 14.10 GW PM-KUSUM/off-grid; up from 100.33 GW in Jan 2025 after a record 44.61 GW addition in FY26) ([MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
    - **Capacity increase:** 2.82 GW in 2014 to 100GW in 2025.
    - Utility scale installation: 18.5 GW
- Rooftop solar (RTS)
- **Market:** Surged from 2.5 GW in FY21 to **25.73 GW cumulative rooftop solar capacity as of March 2026** (with 8.71 GW added in FY26 alone) ([MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
        - **Capacity addition**: India added 1.2 GW of rooftop solar capacity in the first quarter (Q1) of 2025, up 232% year-over-year from 366.5 MW
- **Households:** Over **42 lakh households** benefited from rooftop solar installations till March 2026 (with PM Surya Ghar touching 18.71 lakh installations / 22.7 lakh households in FY26, up from 8.51 lakh installations in FY25) ([MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
        - **New Solar Power Scheme:** Electrifies 100,000 households in tribal areas, providing off-grid solar systems for 63,000 villages, 1,500 multi-purpose centers, and 2,000 public institutions under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan.
        - **PM-Surya Ghar Yojana:** Aims for rooftop solar installations in 10 million households, targeting 40-45 GW capacity by 2027.
- World position
        - 3rd largest solar power producer
        - 5th in solar PV deployment

• Wind energy
    - **Potential:** 695.5 GW at 120 meters and 1,164 GW at 150 meters above ground level
    - **Target:** 500 GW renewable energy by 2030; 140 GW from wind power.
- **Installed capacity:** **56.09 GW as of 31 March 2026** (up from 50.04 GW in April 2025, with a record annual addition of 6.05 GW in FY26) [[MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)]
    - **Potential states:** Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
    - **Funding:** India may add 25 GB wind energy capacity by 2028 but it need Rs 2 lakh crore (CRISIL)
    - **Global position:** 4th after China, United States and Germany.

• Offshore wind energy
    - **Potential:** 70GW across 16 offshore zones of Tamil Nadu and Gujarat coasts.
    - **Current:** As of now, India does not have any active offshore wind projects.
    - **Target:** 37 GW by 2030.

• Hydro energy
    - **Potential:** 1,45,000 MW
    - **Installed capacity:** Share in total power output record low of 8.3% IN 2024, compared to an average of 12.3% over the past decade
- Global Scenario
        - India ranks 4th by undeveloped hydropower potential; 5th by total potential.
        - India exploited 29% of its hydropower potential (US- 80%; EU-70%)
Classification of Hydro projects
- Micro: upto 100 KW
- Mini: 101KW to 2 MW
- Small: 2 MW to 25 MW
- Mega: Hydro projects with installed capacity >= 500 MW
- Thermal Projects with installed capacity >=1500 MW
5. Small Hydro energy
- **Potential:** 20 GW
- **Installed capacity:** **5.17 GW as of 31 March 2026** (up from 5.07 GW; Large Hydro installed capacity stands at 51.41 GW) [[MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)]

• Bioenergy
- **Current capacity:** **11.75 GW as of 31 March 2026** (up from 11.58 GW in April 2025; total Non-Fossil installed capacity reached **283.46 GW**, including **274.68 GW Renewable Energy** and **8.78 GW Nuclear**) [[MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)]

• Hydrogen based energy
    - **Current consumption:** 6 mmtpa

    - **Target:** Green hydrogen production capacity of 5 mn tonnes by 2030 ([National Green Hydrogen mission](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)).
