POLLUTION & WASTE MANAGEMENT

Plastic pollution

• India
        - **Annual:** Generates 9.3 million tonnes of plastic pollution annually.
        - **Daily:** 26,000 tonnes of plastic waste – every day -> equivalent of 26,000 small cars!
        - **Per capita plasti**c waste production (8 kg per year)
        - **Plastic recycling:** Just 8%
        - **Single use plastic waste:** India ranked 3rd globally; contributes to 5.5 million tonnes per year.

• Global
        - **Waste generation:** 268 million tonnes in 2022.
        - **Largest consumers:** China (20%), US (18%), EU (16%), India (6%) and Japan (4%)
        - **Per capita consumption** ->highest in the US at 216 kg per person, Japan (129 kg per person) and EU (87 kg per person).

Air pollution

• World Air Quality Report (2024 & 2025 - IQAir)
- **Rank:** India ranked **6th most polluted country** (out of 143) in the 2025 World Air Quality Report [was 5th in 2024 and 3rd in 2023] ([IQAir 2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries))
- **PM2.5 Reduction:** National average PM2.5 concentration declined further to **48.9 µg/m³ in 2025**, down from 50.6 µg/m³ in 2024 and 54.4 µg/m³ in 2023 ([IQAir 2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries)).
            - **WHO safe limi**t: 5 µg/m³.
- **Delhi & Indian Cities ->** New Delhi remained the **most polluted capital city in the world** for the 8th consecutive year (91.8 µg/m³ in 2024); Loni (UP) was the most polluted city in 2025 at 112.5 µg/m³, and **66 of the world's 100 most polluted cities** (and 13 of top 20 in 2024) are in India ([IQAir 2025/2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries)).
        - **13 of the 20 most polluted cities** in the world are in India.
- **Global (2025 Report):** Top 5 most polluted countries -> Pakistan (67.3 µg/m³), Bangladesh (66.1 µg/m³), Tajikistan (57.3 µg/m³), Chad (53.6 µg/m³), and DR Congo (50.2 µg/m³) [in 2024: Chad (91.8 µg/m³), Bangladesh (78 µg/m³), Pakistan (73.7 µg/m³), Congo (58.2 µg/m³)] ([IQAir 2025/2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries)).

Mercury pollution
- **India-** 2nd largest mercury emitter -> 144.7 tonnes Hg/year
- India imports over 250 metric tonnes of mercury each year
- India leaks > 220 tonnes into the environment from known sources (Toxics Link, a NGO)
- > 70% to 80% of India's mercury emissions due to coal usage.

• Global position
        - Current levels in the atmosphere are up to 500 % above natural levels.
        - **In Oceans:** 200 % above natural levels.
4. Land pollution: 33% of the country’s total geographic area —are affected by soil
degradation, salinity, and vegetation loss.

Noise pollution
- Optimum noise level ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535))
        - 45 dB during the day and 35 dB at night.
        - Anything above 80 dB is hazardous.
    - 12,000 premature deaths and 48,000 new cases of ischaemic heart disease every year (European Environment agency)
    - Noise level of >80 decibels for more than 8 hours a day increases changes in breathing patterns ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535))

Light pollution
- Artificial light increasing by around 2% per year globally.

Biomedical waste
- India generates 743 tonnes of biomedical waste daily and about 640 tonnes is treated ([CPCB report](https://cpcb.nic.in/))

Waste to Energy conversion
- **Total waste:** 65 million tonnes of waste every year;
    - estimated to go up to 165 million tonnes by 2030 and
    - 436 million tonnes by 2050
- Conversion Potential
        - 1700 MW from urban waste (1500 from MSW and 225 MW from sewage) and
        - about 1300 MW from industrial waste [[Ministry of New and Renewable Energy](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)]
    - **Current status:** 75% of municipal waste gets collected; only 22 to 28 percent is processed
    - 12 operational and eight non-operational waste-to-energy plants in India in 10 states as of November 2022.

Solid waste management
- India generated 170,000 tonnes of municipal solid waste per day
    - **Collection and treatment:** About 156,000 tonnes were collected, of which nearly 54 per cent was treated, and
    - **Deposition in landfills:** 24% was deposited in landfills ([CPCB 2024](https://cpcb.nic.in/)).
- Type of waste
        - 50-55% of waste in Indian cities is biodegradable wet waste;
        - 35% is non-biodegradable wet waste; 10% is inert.
    - **Per capita waste generation** -> B/w 0.2 Kg to 0.6 Kg per day in cities with population ranging from 1.0 lakh to 50 lakhs.
    - **Projections**: Indian cities will generate approximately 435 million tonnes of solid waste by 2050 ([MoHUA](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) 2021).

E-Waste

• India
        - 3rd biggest e-waste generator behind China and the U.S.
        - 67% of India's e-waste remains unprocessed ([Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100))

• Global [Global E-waste Monitor 2024 Report]
        - Increase in global e-waste generation, rising from 34 billion (bn) kg in 2010 to 62 bn kg in 2022.
        - Of this 62 bn kg, only 13.8 bn kg is documented as ‘formally collected and recycled in an environmentally sound manner’.
        - 62 million tons of “e-waste” was generated in 2022-> enough to fill tractor-trailers that could be lined up bumper to bumper around globe.

Circular economy
- **India:** India's circular economy could touch $45 billion by 2030.
- **Global:** Transition to a circular economy could generate $4.5 trillion in additional economic output globally by 2030.

content_markdown:
WATER & ITS CONSERVATION

Water Scarcity
- **Water Scarcity**: As per World Bank, Annual per-capita water availability
    - < 1700 m³: Water Stressed condition
    - < 1000 m³: Water Scarcity condition (India =: Around 1500 m³ (CWC))
- **Global Scenario**: Water scarcity affects more than 40% of the global population
- India’s Scenario
        - 18% of world population lives in India but it has just 4% of world’s water resources.
        - India is the second-largest consumer of water, using 20.1 per cent of global water resources.
        - It ranks 133rd in water availability per capita
    - **Per Capita Use (India):** Average annual per capita water availability for the year 2021 was 1,486 cubic meters ([Ministry of Jal Shakti](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2220203®=3&lang=1))
    - **Projected water demand**: Per capita water use is projected to increase from 85 litres per capita per day (lpcd) in 2000 to 125 lpcd by 2025 and 170 lpcd by 2050.
    - **Access**: 50% has no access to safe water.
    - **Deaths**: Around 2 Lac/year (due to lack of access to safe water)
    - **Economic Burden**: Loss of 6% of GDP

Water Pollution
- **Surface Water Pollution**: 80% of surface water is polluted
- **Pollution Levels**: 70% water resources are polluted ([Composite Water Management Index](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-03/Composite-Water-Management-Index.pdf))
- **Source of River Pollution**:
    - 80% of river pollution -> untreated waste
    - 20% of river pollution -> Industries

Groundwater Crisis
- India is the largest groundwater user globally (26% of world).
- **Annual groundwater extraction:** **247.22 BCM in 2025** (245.64 BCM in 2024; 241.34 BCM in 2023), out of 407.75 BCM annual extractable groundwater resources ([CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resource Assessment 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf)).
- The country's **Stage of Ground Water Extraction (SoE) is 60.63% in 2025** (60.47% in 2024; 59.26% in 2023) ([CGWB 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf)).
- India consumes more groundwater than the US and China combined
- Annual groundwater recharge -> **448.52 BCM in 2025** (up from 446.90 BCM in 2024 and 432 BCM in 2017) ([Ministry of Jal Shakti](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2220203®=3&lang=1) / [CGWB 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf))
- Ground Water Table -> 0.3 ↓/Year
- Dependency
        - 62% of irrigation needs are met through groundwater.
        - 85% of rural and 50% of urban water supply depend on groundwater.
- **10.8% of groundwater assessment units (730 out of 6,762 units) are over-exploited in 2025** (down from 17.2% in 2017), while **73.14% (4,946 units) are in the Safe category** (up from 62.6% in 2017) ([CGWB 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf))
    - GW depletion rate could triple by 2080, if Indian farmers continued to draw groundwater at the current rate.
- Annual Groundwater Quality Report 2024
        - Largest user of groundwater
        - Largest area under groundwater irrigation in the world.
        - **Uses**
            - 87% of extracted groundwater in agriculture and
            - 11% is used for domestic purposes.

Ocean pollution
- As of 2025, 75 to 199 million tonnes of plastic and waste in our oceans.
- 171 trillion pieces of plastic estimated to be floating in the world's oceans.

Oil pollution
- Ten oil spills of more than seven tonnes were recorded from tanker incidents in 2024

Urban water crisis
- 48% of India’s urban water supply comes from groundwater (CSE)
- 40% of people in urban areas in India don't get tap water [[National Sample Survey Office](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports)]
- By 2030 India’s water demand would be double due to rapid urbanization and little infra planning (UN report)

        - **Literacy Rate:** 74.04% ([2011 census](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/)); 77% (National Statistical Office (NSO)) -> nearly 8 out of 10 people can read and write.

        - **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM):** Declared rural India Open Defecation Free (ODF) in October 2019.

content_markdown:
PRE-COLONIAL PERIOD & CHRONOLOGY

• Culture: Artefacts smuggling
        - The US returned 1,400 looted artifacts, valued at nearly $10 million, to India (Nov 2024)
        - India reclaimed 297 antiquities during PM Modi's recent US visit, raising the total recoveries since 2014 to 640 (Sep 2024).

• Economy during Mughal period
- GDP in the 16th century (1600 AD) -> ~22.5–25.1% of the world economy - 2nd largest in the world ([Angus Maddison, The World Economy: Historical Statistics](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/)).
        - Annual revenue of Akbar's treasury in 1600 AD at £17.5 million (in contrast to the entire treasury of Great Britain two hundred years later in 1800 AD, which totalled £16 million).
        - India experienced unprecedented prosperity in history.

• Advent of Europeans
        - the Portuguese, the first Europeans to come to India (1498), were also the last to leave this land (1961).
        - **Third Anglo-Mysore War**: Tipu Sultan had to pay Rs.3 Crore as war indemnity. He also had to surrender 2 of his sons as surety to the British till he paid his due.

content_markdown:
BRITISH COLONIAL ECONOMY

• Economic drain by British
        - **Scholars**:
            - **Romesh Chandra Dutt**: In early 20th century ≈ £20 million flew out of India.
            - **MG Ranade**: In his book "Essay on Indian Economics," he claimed that Britishers drained more than one-third of India's wealth into England.
            - **Dadabhai Naoroji**: India's tax burden in 1886 was 14.3% of total revenue, significantly higher than England's 6.93%.
            - **Angus Maddison** (British economist): India's share of the world income went from 27% in 1700 AD (compared to Europe's share of 23%) to 3% in 1950.
        - **Reports**:
            - **'Takers Not Makers: The Unjust Poverty and Unearned Wealth of Colonial Inheritance' report, 2025 ([Oxfam](https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/takers-not-makers-unjust-poverty-and-unearned-wealth-colonialism))**:
                - Wealth Drain during Colonial Period -> Between 1765 and 1900, UK drained $64.82 trillion from India, with $33.8 trillion going to the top 10%.
        - **India and its Contradictions**: In the 18th century, India became a land of contrasts because extreme poverty and extreme luxury existed side by side.

• Famines
        - Between 1730 to 1947 🢥 31 famines, loss of life of 8.5 cr. Indians
        - In 1770, there was a terrible Famine in Bengal which killed about 1 Crore people.

• Land Revenue systems
        - **Permanent Settlement**:
            - Covered 20% of British India
            - The state received 10/11th of the rent the zamindars received from the peasantry, with only 1/11th going to the zamindars themselves.
            - Between 1794 and 1819, **68%** of zamindari land was sold in Bengal.
        - **Ryotwari System**:
            - Covered 51% area of British India.
            - Revenue was fixed at very high rate (45-50%)

• State of Industry
        - Up until 1750, India produced about 25% of the world's industrial output.
        - India had a 25% share of the global textile trade in the early 18th century.
        - By 1664, the English East India Company imported more than 750,000 pieces of cotton goods from India, which accounted for 73 per cent of the Company’s total trade.

• Infrastructure
        - On April 16, 1853 -> first railway line in India spanning upto 34 kilometers between Boribandar (Bombay) to Thane.
        - Built 6000 kms of track by 1869 and 45,000 km of track by 1905 with the help of private enterprises.
- **Railway length** = ~69,439 route km (~1.32 lakh track km) today ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) --> ~53,000–54,000 km built during British rule before 1947 ([Ministry of Railways](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).

content_markdown:
FREEDOM STRUGGLE & MOVEMENTS

• Revolt of 1857
        - **European Soldier to Indian soldier ratio**: 1:2
- Revolt of 1857 -> Proportion of Europeans to Indians was carefully fixed at 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay Armies to avoid another revolt (Peel Commission, 1859 / [NCERT](https://ncert.nic.in/)).
        - In Awadh, more **than 20,000 taluqdars had their estates confiscated**

• Bengal Partition (1905)
        - **Reason given for Partition**: Population of 78 million Bengal had become too big to be administered.

• Jallianwala Bagh
        - House of Lords endorsed Reginald Dyer’s action and the British public showed solidarity with him by helping collect **30,000 pounds** for him for his atrocities in Jallianwala Bagh.

• Non-Cooperation Movement (1920 to 1922)
        - 1st nationwide movement launched by Gandhiji in 1920 during British rule.
        - **During Non-cooperation Movement**:
            - Thousands of students left schools and colleges and joined only 800 national schools and colleges.
            - Rs 1 crore were raised for Tilak Swaraj Fund by August 1921, and 1 crore/50 lakhs members got enrolled in Congress.
        - **Consequence of Non-Cooperation Movement**: The import of foreign goods halved between 1921 and 1922.

• Home Rule League Movement
        - Tilak’s Home Rule League had 6 Branches while Annie Besant’s Home rule League had 200+ Branches.

• Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)
        - Gandhi along with a band of 78 members of Sabarmati Ashram, marched from his headquarters in Ahmedabad for 240 miles.
        - On April 23, 1930, the arrest of Congress leaders in the NWFP led to the participation of a 92% Muslim population.
        - Gandhi’s Eleven demands -> Reduce Rupee-Sterling Exchange Ratio to 1s 4d: Called for a change in the exchange rate between the Indian rupee and the British pound to benefit Indian traders and businesses.

• 1937 Elections
        - 1937 elections were held in 11 provinces- Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar, Orissa, Assam, NWFP, Bengal, Punjab, Bombay and Sindh
        - In 1937 elections, An estimated 30.1 million persons, including 4.25 million women, had acquired the right to vote (**12% of the total population**), and 15.5 millions of these, including 917,000 women, participated to exercise their franchise.
        - In 1937 elections, Among the 864 seats assigned “general” constituencies, Congress **contested 739** and won 617.

content_markdown:
COLONIAL POLICIES & DEVELOPMENT

• Administrative Reforms
        - **Cornawallis Reforms**:
            - all higher posts in administration worth **more than 500 pounds a year** in salary could be held by Englishmen only.
            - Charter Act of 1793 had reserved all posts worth 500 pounds per annum for the covenant servants of the Company.
            - Salary of the Collector of a district was raised to Rs. 1500 a month and 1 per cent commission on the revenue collected from his district.
        - **Viscount Lee Commission** recommendations (1924): Parity between Indians and Europeans: To be achieved **50:50 parity** in 15 years.
        - **Morley-Minto Reforms**: number of members in the Central Legislative Council was raised from 16 to 60.
        - **Provinces**: 3 provinces in 1773 to 17 provinces in 1947.

• Social Development
- **Status of illiteracy**: ~94% in 1911 (~6% literacy) and ~92% in 1921 (~8% literacy; ~84% illiteracy at Independence in 1947) ([Census of British India](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/) / [NCERT](https://ncert.nic.in/))
        - **Number of Universities**:
            - **1857:** 3 (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras)
            - **1947:** 19 universities, ~500 colleges
        - **Age of Consent Act(1891):** Raised age of consent for girls from 10 to 12 years.
        - **Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929):** Minimum marriage age: 14 (girls) and 18 (boys).
        - **Gandhi ji campaign for untouchability**: Gandhi’s campaign against untouchability which covered 12,500 miles and lasted for nine months.
        - **Poona Pact**: Number of seats reserved for the depressed classes in provincial legislatures would be increased from 71 in the Award to 147; and to 18% of the total in central legislature.
        - **Rabindranath Tagore** wrote around 2230 songs.

• Decline in violence and deaths
- **Violence:** Maoist-perpetrated violence fell from peak levels to 375 incidents in 2024, **234 in 2025**, and **33 in 2026 (till 21 July 2026)** (>81% reduction) ([MHA July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2291043®=48&lang=1)).

- reduced from 126 districts in 2013 to 90 in April 2018, 70 in July 2021, 38 in April 2024, **08 in December 2025**, and **“zero” LWE-affected districts in March/April 2026** (with 37 'Legacy & Thrust' districts and 1 'District of Concern' under continued support) ([MHA July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2291043®=48&lang=1)).

- **Fortified Police stations:** **663 Fortified Police Stations (FPS)** constructed across erstwhile LWE-affected States as of July 2026 (up from 400) ([MHA July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2291043®=48&lang=1)).

• Nepal
- **Bilateral Trade**: $8.66 billion in FY 2022-23; India's merchandise exports to Nepal stood at **$7.45 billion ($7,447.11 million) in FY 2025-26** ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))

        - **MOUs**: India, Nepal ink 10 MoUs worth Nepalese Rs.625 million for community development projects (April 2025)
        - **Line of Credit**: Line of credit of $680 million by India to fund three major transmission corridors in Nepal - Bheri Corridor, Nijgadh-Inaruwa Corridor and Gandak-Nepalgunj Corridor.

• Bhutan
- **Bilateral trade**: $1.34 billion in FY 2022-23; India's merchandise exports to Bhutan reached **$1.25 billion ($1,252.86 million) in FY 2025-26** ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))

- **Development assistance**: India doubled assistance to **₹10,000 crore for Bhutan's 13th Five-Year Plan (2024–2029)**, up from ₹4,500–5,000 crore in the 12th Plan ([MEA](https://www.mea.gov.in/))
        - **Foreign direct investments**: India contributes to 50% of the Bhutan's total foreign direct investment (FDI)

• Pakistan
        - **Bilateral Trade**: From 2018 to 2024, bilateral trade fell from $2.41bn to $1.2bn.
        - **Trade Relations**:
            - India withdrew MFN status (after Pulwama)
            - Pakistan suspended Bilateral Trade (After the August 370 decision)
            - India consists of 3% of Pakistan’s total trade.
            - Pakistani exports to India plummeted from $547.5m in 2019 to just $480,000 in 2024. India Exports to Pakistan was US$1.18 Billion during 2024

• Myanmar
        - **Bilateral Trade**: $1.33 billion in FY23-24
        - **Development assistance**: India has already extended $2 billion in soft loans
        - **Indian companies**: Essar, GAIL, and ONGC Videsh Ltd. have invested in Myanmar’s energy sector.
        - **Exports**: India Exports: US$609.18 million during 2024
        - **Imports**: Imports from Myanmar: US$1.52 Billion during 2024

• Sri Lanka
- **Bilateral trade**: India is Sri Lanka's largest trading partner ($5.5 billion in FY 2023-24; India's merchandise exports to Sri Lanka reached **$5.52 billion ($5,516.83 million) in FY 2025-26**) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)).

        - **Exports**: US$4.72 Billion in 2024
        - **Imports**: US$967.76 million in 2024
        - **FDI**: investments of USD 2.25 billion till 2023.
        - **Development assistance**:
            - Assistance of USD 14.9 million by India to undertake a Signaling System in the Maho Anuradhapura segment of Sri Lankan railways.
            - India has extended over USD 7 billion in credit and USD 780 million in grants to Sri Lanka.
            - India extended a $400 million currency swap post-COVID and has invested over $2.25 billion in Sri Lanka
            - A USD 400 million currency swap through the Reserve Bank of India.

• Bangladesh
        - **Bilateral Trade**: USD 14.01 billion (2023-24)
        - **Trade Partner**: Bangladesh is India’s largest trading partner in South Asia.
        - **Exports**: India’s exports: USD 11.06 billion
        - **Imports**: India’s imports: USD 1.8 billion.
        - **Trade Agreements**: As SAFTA members, India and Bangladesh receive preferential tariff concessions.

        - **Exports**: India's exports: USD 355.45 million in 2023-24.
        - **Imports**: India’s imports: USD 642.29 million in 2023-24.

INDIA'S MAJOR BILATERAL RELATIONS

• USA
- **Bilateral trade**: $131.84 billion in FY 2024-25 ($129 billion in CY 2024; India recorded a $34.4 billion trade surplus with the US in FY 2025-26 and $40.89 billion in FY 2024-25) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)).
            - **Target**: Mission 500-> $500 billion by 2030.
- **Largest trading partner**: The U.S. was India's largest trading partner in FY 2024-25, while China surpassed the US to become the largest trading partner in FY 2025-26 ([MoC&I 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)).
        - **Investments**: Indian companies have invested $7.35 billion in the US
        - **Defense Relations**: US is India’s 4th largest arms supplier.
        - **Defense agreements**: GSOMIA (2002), LEMOA (2016), COMCASA (2018), BECA (2020)

• China
- **Bilateral trade**: Surged in FY 2025-26 (imports from China rose 16% to **$131.63 billion** in FY 2025-26; bilateral trade was $118.4B–$127.7B in FY24/FY25) ([MoC&I 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
- **Trade deficit**: Trade deficit with China widened from $85.1 billion (FY24) and $99.2 billion (FY25) to an all-time high of **$112.6 billion in FY 2025-26** ([MoC&I 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
        - **Exports**: Top Exports to China: Iron ore, refined petroleum, cyclic hydrocarbons and organic chemicals.
        - **Imports**: Top Imports from China: Electrical machinery, telecom instruments, mineral fuels including oil, fertilizers, organic chemicals, computer hardware
        - **Bilateral Economic Presence**:
            - Chinese Companies in India: 174 registered companies
            - Indian companies in China: 54

• Russia
- **Bilateral trade**: Reached ~$65.7–$68.7 billion in FY24/FY25 (targeting $100 billion bilateral trade by 2030) ([MEA](https://www.mea.gov.in/) / [MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
        - **Investment**: India's investments in Russia were estimated to be USD 16 billion. Russian Investments in India total around USD 20 billion.
        - **Energy Security**: India's Russian crude oil imports will hit close to 1.8 million barrels per day in May 2025.
        - **Line of credit**: India extended a $1 billion credit line for Russia’s Far East development.
        - **Historical Ties**: Russia historically provided around 47% of India’s arms imports, down from 65% historically.

• Canada
        - **Bilateral Trade**: $12 billion in 2023.
        - **Exports**: India’s exports: $3.80 billion
        - **Imports**: India’s imports: $5.56 billion.
        - **Investment**: Canadian Pension Funds have cumulatively invested over $ 75 billion in India
        - **Diaspora**: ~1.8 million; > 3% of its total population.
        - **FDI**: Canada is the 18th largest foreign investor in India; invested $3,306 million between April 2000 and March 2023.
        - **CEPA**: In 2010, Canada and India launched negotiations toward a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
        - **Top Exports from India**: The main items exported by India to Canada are Jewellery, Cotton yarn, Organic chemicals, Coffee, Spices, Iron and steel articles, Textiles, Carpets, Floor spreads, and processed foods.
        - **Top Imports to India**: The main products exported from Canada to India were Dried Legumes, Coal Briquettes, and Potassic Fertilizers. ### Section Group: Global Geopolitics & Indian Diaspora

- **Bilateral Trade**: Crossed **$100 billion in FY 2024-25** (up from $83.7 billion in FY 2023-24; India's merchandise exports to the UAE under CEPA reached **$37.36 billion ($37,359.11 million) in FY 2025-26**) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)).
        - **Trade Partner**: India is the UAE's second-largest trading partner
        - **Crude oil**: UAE is India’s 4th largest source of crude oil and the 2nd largest source of LNG & LPG.
        - **Strategic Oil Reserves**: UAE is the only nation in the region to offer to store strategic oil reserves in India.
        - **Exports**: $48 billion in FY2023-24. Non-oil exports reached $27.4 billion.
        - **Imports**: USD 50.51 billion
        - **Remittances**: About $14 billion a year.
        - **Diaspora**: around 30% of the UAE's population; 3.5 million (largest ethnic group in the country)
- **Agreements**: India and UAE implemented **CEPA (May 2022)** and **Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT, 2024)**; India also implemented the **India–Oman CEPA on 1 June 2026** granting duty-free access to 99.38% of Indian exports by value ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)).

• Saudi Arabia
        - **Bilateral Trade**: ~USD 43 billion (2023-24).
        - **Trade Rank**: India is Saudi Arabia's 2nd largest trading partner, and Saudi Arabia is India's 5th.
        - **Crude oil imports**: India's 3rd largest source of crude oil and petroleum products (2023–24).
        - **Remittances**: 6.7% of India's total inward remittances.
        - **Investments**: Saudi Arabia has invested around USD 10 billion in India so far and in 2019, it announced plans to invest USD 100 billion more.
        - **Vision 2030 Synergy**: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 aims to diversify its economy, and India is seen as a key partner in this transformation

• Israel Palestine
        - **Israel Bilateral Trade**: USD 10.1 billion in FY 2022-2023.
        - **Israel Trade Rank**: India is Israel’s 2nd trading partner in Asia and the 9th largest globally.
        - **Israel Diaspora**: Approximately 85,000 Jews of Indian origin live in Israel.
        - **Israel Diamond Trade**: Trade in diamonds constitutes about 50% of bilateral trade.
        - **Palestine Bilateral Trade**: $67.77 million in 2020
        - **Palestine Aid**: India has donated around $141 million in various forms of aid to the Palestinian Authority, including $39 million in administrative support.

• Qatar
        - **Bilateral Trade**: USD 14.08 billion (2023-24)
            - **Target**: Aim to double bilateral trade from $14 billion to $28 billion in the next five years.
        - **LNG**: Qatar is India's largest LNG supplier, providing over 40% of imports.
        - **Exports and Imports**: In 2023-24, the country's imports from Qatar stood at USD 12.34 billion, while its exports were only USD 1.7 billion.
        - **Exports Detail**: India's primary exports to Qatar include Basmati rice (USD 124 million), articles of iron and steel (USD 200 million), and machinery (USD 106 million)
        - **Imports Detail**: A large portion (85 per cent) of India's imports from Qatar comprises LNG (USD 6.3 billion), butane, propane mostly for LPG production (USD 3.1 billion), and petroleum crude (USD 1.1 billion)

• Persian Gulf
        - **Trade**: USD 161.59 billion during 2023-24
        - **Oil and Gas**: Around 60% of India’s crude oil imports come from GCC countries.

content_markdown:
INDIA-EUROPE

• United Kingdom
        - **Bilateral Trade**: $57 billion in 2024
        - **Trade Relations**:
            - India was the UK's 11th largest trading partner in 2024, accounting for 2.4% of total UK trade.
            - Exports and Imports: India's exports stood at $8.5 billion and imports were $3.7 billion.
            - FDI: India is second-largest investor in terms of the number of FDI projects for the UK for five consecutive years.
            - Economic asymmetry: India's larger economy ($4 trillion) contrasts with UK's higher per capita income ($50,000 vs. $3,000).
- **India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA / FTA, effective 15 July 2026 - [MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)):**
            - It aims to double trade between the world’s fifth and sixth-largest economies in goods and services, increasing it from $60 billion currently to $120 billion by 2030.
- Grants zero-duty access for 99% of Indian exports to the UK (India's merchandise exports to the UK reached **$13.44 billion ($13,444.19 million) in FY 2025-26**; additionally, the **India–EFTA TEPA entered into force in October 2025** offering 99.6% Indian export coverage) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)).
            - Tariffs on automobiles will drop significantly, from over 100 percent to 10 percent under a special quota system
            - Expected outcomes:
                - ↑ UK’s GDP by £3.3 billion by 2035 and double bilateral trade from US$60 billion in 2024 to US$100 billion by 2030.
                - ↑ bilateral trade, with projected annual growth of around 15 percent until calendar year 2030 [Care Edge report].

• Spain
        - **Bilateral trade**: $9.9 billion in 2023
        - **Trade Partner**: Spain is India’s 6th largest trade partner in Europe
        - **Investments**: Spain is 16th largest investor in India, with $4.2 billion in FDI (April 2000 – June 2024) with over 280 Spanish companies active in India.
        - **Indian Investments**: Indian companies have invested over US$ 900 million in Spain predominantly in the IT services, pharmaceuticals, and logistics sectors

• Germany
        - **Bilateral trade**: Germany is India's largest trade partner in Europe, with bilateral trade reaching US$ 33.33 billion in 2023.
        - **Trading partner**: Germany continued to be the 12th largest trading partner for India also in 2023-24.
        - **Exports and imports**: Indian exports to Germany rose to US$10.1 billion, while German imports to India stood at around US$14.9 billion.
        - **Foreign Direct Investments**: Germany is the 9th largest foreign direct investor in India, with a cumulative FDI of US$ 14.5 billion, with around 1,800 German companies operating in India.
        - **Development cooperation**: The total volume of bilateral technical and financial cooperation by the end of 2023 amounted to about Euro 24 billion.

• France
        - **Bilateral Trade**: Trade: USD 13 billion in FY2022-23
        - **EU Partner**: France is India's 11th largest trading partner in the European Union, with bilateral trade exceeding $12 billion in 2023.
        - **Exports**: US$ 7 billion
        - **Imports**: US$5.82 billion

        - **Exports and Imports**: India's imports were $21.13 billion, while exports were only $6.41 billion.

• Japan
- **Bilateral Trade**: Stood at $22.85 billion in FY24 (India's merchandise exports to Japan under CEPA reached **$6.04 billion ($6,039.50 million) in FY 2025-26**) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1)).

        - **Economic Rank**: India surpassed Japan to become the 4th largest economy in the world
        - **Agreement**: India-Japan CEPA (2011) covers trade, services, investments, and IPRs.

• Australia
- **Bilateral Trade**: ~$24.1 billion merchandise trade in FY 2024-25 (~$30 billion total trade; India's merchandise exports to Australia under ECTA stood at **$7.28 billion ($7,284.17 million) in FY 2025-26**) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [PIB July–Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2300733))
        - **Trade Rank**: India is Australia's fifth largest trading partner
        - **Exports and Imports**: India's goods exports reaching $7.94 billion and imports at $16.15 billion.

content_markdown:
MULTILATERAL

• BRICS
- **GDP**: Expanded BRICS+ accounts for ~37.3% of world GDP in PPP terms (compared to EU's 14.5% and G7's 29.3%) ([IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/Publications/WEO) / BRICS 2024-25)
        - **Population**: BRICS countries collectively account for 46% of the global population, with significant populations in China and India
        - **Total Intra-BRICS Trade**: US$614.8 billion as of 2022.
        - **Powerful driver for the global economy**:
            - Over the past decade, the combined BRICS GDP has grown by 179%.
            - Total trade of the member nations has expanded by 94%.

• SAARC
        - **Geography**: 3% of the world's land area
        - **Population**: 21% of the world's population
        - **Global GDP**: 5.21% (US$4.47 trillion) of the global economy, as of 2021.
        - **Intra SAARC Trade**: Their intra-regional trade stands at just 5.8%.

• BIMSTEC
        - **Population**: Home to around 1.5 billion people that constitute around 22% of the global population
        - **GDP**: Combined Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of USD 3.8 trillion.
        - **Intra-BIMSTEC trade**: Around 7% of the total trade among member countries as of the latest data.
        - **Trade Volume**: The total intra-BIMSTEC trade volume was about $60 billion in 2023
        - **Trade potential**: The Bay of Bengal is the largest bay in the world and is the route for about 25 percent of global trade.

• G20
        - **Population**: Almost two-thirds of the global population
        - **Global GDP**: 75% of global trade, and 85% of the world's GDP.
        - **CO2 emissions**: The G20 countries are responsible for approximately 80% of global carbon dioxide emissions.
        - **Military spending**: The G20 countries account for approximately 85% of global military spending.
        - **Foreign direct investment**: The G20 countries account for approximately 80% of global foreign direct investment.

• QUAD
        - **Combined GDP**: The combined GDP of the QUAD countries is approximately 35.08% of the world GDP.
        - **Combined Population**: The combined population of the QUAD countries is approximately 23.78% of the world population.
        - **Combined Defense Spending**: The combined defense spending of the QUAD countries is approximately 46.88% of the world defense spending.

• IPEF
        - **Total GDP**: The combined GDP -> USD 33.99 trillion.
        - **Total Population**: The total population of these countries is around 2.451 billion people.
        - **Total Trade Volume**: The total trade volume of the member countries is about USD 11.705 trillion.

• SCO
        - **Combined GDP**: The combined GDP -> 23% of the world GDP.
        - **Population**: 42% of the world population.
        - **Defense Spending**: The combined defense spending is approximately 20.61% of the world defense spending.

• NATO
        - **Combined GDP**: The combined GDP of the major NATO countries is approximately 37.90% of the world GDP.
        - **Combined Population**: The combined population is approximately 7.34% of the world population.
        - **Combined Defense Spending**: The combined defense spending is approximately 48.93% of the world defense spending.
        - **Combined Budget**: Combined total budget: $1.47 trillion in 2024
        - **Intra-NATO Trade**: Combined intra-NATO trade: Approximately $3.3 trillion (2023)

• WTO
        - **GDP**: Estimates suggest that WTO members contribute approximately 98% of world GDP.
        - **Population**: WTO members represent approximately 96% of the world population.
        - **Trade**: Combined Intra-WTO Trade: Approximately $33 trillion (75% of global trade)

• RCEP
        - **Status**: It is the world’s largest free trade agreement by members’ GDP.
        - **GDP**: Combined GDP of RCEP Countries: Approximately $30.53 trillion (29.36% of world GDP)
        - **Population**: Combined Population of RCEP Countries: Approximately 2317 million (28.96% of world population)
        - **Defense**: Combined Defense Spending of RCEP Countries: Approximately $485.3 billion (21.67% of world defense spending)
        - **Trade**: Intra-RCEP Trade: Approximately $13.2 trillion (30% of global trade)

• NAM
        - **Population**: Combined Population: Approximately 4.8 billion (2023)
        - **3 Largest Countries by Population**:
            - India: Approximately 1.42 billion
            - Indonesia: Approximately 280 million
            - Pakistan: Approximately 243 million\
        - **GDP**: Approximate Combined GDP: $28 trillion (estimation based on major members)
        - **World Share**: Approximately 26.92% of world GDP

• G7
        - **Population**: Combined Population: 10% of world population
        - **Share**: Contribution: 40% of global economy
        - **GDP**: Combined GDP: Approximately $45.62 trillion

• IORA
        - **Population**: Approximately 2.7 billion
        - **3 Largest Countries**:
            - India: 1.42 billion
            - Indonesia: 280 million
            - Bangladesh: 170 million
        - **GDP**: Combined GDP: Approximately $10 trillion
        - **World Share**: Approximately 9.62% of world GDP

• India's contribution to UNPKF
- **Troops**: Contributed **>2,90,000 troops** cumulatively (up from >2,53,000), the largest cumulative contributor from any country ([MEA](https://www.mea.gov.in/) / [UN Peacekeeping 2025-26](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en/india)).
- **Missions**: Participated in **51+ out of 71 UN peacekeeping missions** established since 1948 ([MEA](https://www.mea.gov.in/) / UN).
        - **Deployments**: Currently, Indian Armed Forces are deployed across 9 countries in peacekeeping missions like UN Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) (Golan), UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNFIL), etc.
        - **Women Contingent**: First country to deploy All Women Contingent in 2007 to United Nations Mission in Liberia (UNMIL).

SIGNIFICANT PROVISIONS

• Status of Refugees
- **Recognized Refugees:** >2 Lac ([UNHCR](https://www.unhcr.org/in/))
- **Non Recognized refugees:** 20 million, mostly from Bangladesh.
- **Internally Displaced People:** more than 5 lakh
- **International Scenario:** UN - over 100 million migrants living outside their country of birth in 2022.
- **Rohingyas:** 22,500 Rohingya refugees currently reside in India ([UNHCR](https://www.unhcr.org/in/))
- **Kashmiri pandits:** up to 3 lakh
- **Bru refugees:** 30,000 in Tripura - from Mizoram.

• Reservations in India
- **OBC/SC/ST:** 27% / 15% / 7.5%
- **Reservation Limit:** 50% - Indra Sawhney v Union of India (1992)
    - **EWS** reservation is outside this limit.
- **Miniscule Representation of SC/ST at Higher Levels:** SC/ST representation at Secretary, Joint Sec. level in Centre stands at 4% and 4.9% resp. (Rajya Sabha data from 2022)
- **Prevalence of Untouchability:** National Campaign for Dalit Human Rights - 38% of government schools require students to have lunch separately.

• OBC Reservation
- **Dominance of Few Section:** 24.95% of jobs and seats to just 10 OBC communities.
- **97% of all jobs and educational seats** – to 25% of all sub-castes classified as OBCs.
- **0 Representation**: 983 OBC communities (37%) - zero representation in jobs and educational institutions.

• Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC)
- **Households:** 24.49 cr - 17.97 cr living in **villages**

**Landlessness**
        - 56% of rural households do not have access to agricultural land.
        - 5.37cr(29.97%) rural households are "landless" & rely on manual labour.
    - **SC/ST Families:** 21.53% of village families (3.86 cr)
    - **Illiteracy:** 36% of the rural population (884 million) is illiterate > than the 32% reported in 2011 Census
    - **Poverty:** Urban Households vs Rural households:: 35% vs 60%
    - **Manual Scavenging:** 1.80 Lakh households

• Sedition in India
- **No. of cases:** 701 cases of sedition and offences against the State from 2018 to 2022
- **Rate of Conviction:** 33.3% in 2020 ([NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/))

• Preventive Detention
- **Rise in Arrests:** 1.1 lakh people were arrested and detained under preventive detention laws in 2021 - 23.7% rise over 2020 ([NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/))

• Internet Freedom (Freedom on the Net Report 2024 & 2025 - Freedom House)
- Global internet freedom declined for the **15th consecutive year in 2025** (14th in 2024) ([Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2025](https://freedomhouse.org/sites/default/files/2025-11/Freedom_on_the_Net_2025_Digital.pdf)).
- Iceland -> ‘freest online environment’ in the world
- India -> classified in the **‘partly free’** category (score 50–51 out of 100 in 2024–2025) ([Freedom House 2025](https://freedomhouse.org/sites/default/files/2025-11/Freedom_on_the_Net_2025_Digital.pdf)).

• Internet shutdowns
- **India:** 84 shutdowns (Highest in any democracy) affecting 16 states and territories. ([Access Now 2024 report](https://www.accessnow.org/internet-shutdowns-2024/))
- **Economic cost:** shutdowns reportedly cost India total $1.9 billion and $118 million in foreign investment in the first half of 2023 alone.
    - In 2020, India suffered losses of $2.8 billion due to 129 separate instances of internet suspension.
    - Internet Society’s NetLoss Calculator-> a single-day shutdown can push up to 379 people into unemployment in India.
- **Global:** 296 shutdowns were recorded across 54 countries in 2024, an increase from 283 in 2023.

• Capital Punishment
- **World:** More than 2/3rd countries - abolished [Amnesty international].
- **Prevalent in Asia:** India, China, Iran etc. where 60% population of the world lives [Law commission].
- **India:** **561 prisoners on death row** by end of 2023 (up from 544 as of Dec 31, 2022; highest in nearly two decades) ([Project 39A, NLU Delhi](https://www.project39a.com/) / [NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/)).

• Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019
- **Citizenship to 6 non-Muslim communities:** Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians
- **Date:** who entered India on or before 31st December, 2014

FEDERALISM

• Finances
- **Tax Devolution:** **15th Finance Commission (2021-26)** recommended **41%** vertical share for states in the divisible pool; in Union Budget 2026-27, the Government provided **₹1.4 lakh crore to States as Finance Commission Grants** for FY 2026-27 based on **16th Finance Commission** recommendations ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).
- **Borrowing Limit:** Central Government enhanced the borrowing limit of state governments from 3% to 5% of their GSDP.
- **GST compensation cess:** might have a ₹1.37 lakh crore shortfall by March 31 due to ₹50,000 crore interest on Covid loans

• State Finances (RBI State Finances Report 2024-25 & Economic Survey 2025-26)
- **Consolidated Gross Fiscal Deficit (GFD) of States:** Contained around ~2.8% of GDP during FY22–FY24, and edged up to **3.2% of GDP in FY25** (with State capital outlay maintained around ~2.4–2.6% of GDP supported by SASCI) ([RBI State Finances Report](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/AnnualPublications.aspx?head=State%20Finances%20:%20A%20Study%20of%20Budgets) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
        - **Revenue Deficit:** States maintained the revenue deficit at 0.2% of GDP during 2021-22 to 2023-24.
        - **Expenditure quality improved:** Capital outlay, expenditure that leads to creation of physical/financial assets, increased to 2.6% of GDP in 2023-24 from 2.2% in 2022-23.

• Language in India
- **2011 Census:** listed 1,369 ‘mother tongues’ in the country. Hindi is only one among them (mother tongue of only 26% population)
- **121 languages (22 scheduled languages)** spoken by 10,000 or more people in India
- People’s Linguistic Survey of India - **220 Indian languages have** disappeared in the last 50 years, and that another 150 could vanish in the next half century

content_markdown:
JUDICIARY

• Judges to Population Ratio
- **~15–21 judges per million population** (15 working judges per million in India Justice Report 2025; ~21 sanctioned judges per million in Department of Justice data)
    - 150 per million – USA
    - Law Commission (India) -> 50 per million

• Low Female Representation
        - **Supreme Court:** Till date, only 11 female judges in Supreme Court
        - **High Court:** 11.5% Judges are female
        - **Subordinate courts:** 30% Judges are women
        - **Female Advocates:** Out of 1.7 million registered, only 15% are women

• Huge Pendency
        - **Supreme Court:** 82,445 pending cases (Jan 2025)
- **High Courts and Subordinate courts:** **>5.1 crore pending cases** across District/Subordinate Courts (~4.5+ crore) and High Courts (~62.98 lakh as of April 2025), plus ~82,000+ in Supreme Court ([NJDG](https://njdg.ecourts.gov.in/) / [India Justice Report 2025](https://indiajusticereport.org/files/IJR%204_Full%20Report_English_Low.pdf))
        - **Extent of Problem**
            - **1,514 cases in High Courts and 1,390 in subordinate** and district courts have been pending **for over 50 years.**
            - In **subordinate courts, more than 50 per cent of cases** have been pending for over three years.
    - **Government the Largest Litigant:** involvement of the Indian government as the largest litigant, contributing to 50% of pending cases.
    - **Justice Delayed:** At the current disposal rate if no new cases added; Supreme Court - 1.3 years and High Courts and Subordinate Courts – 3 years.
        - HC - 21% cases pending for over 10 years
        - Subordinate Courts - 23% cases for over five years

• Infrastructure Deficiency
        - **Lack of Courtrooms:** shortage of 4,200 courtrooms for judges across the country (Centre for Research and Planning of Supreme Court of India report)
        - **District courts**: ~37.7% of Judicial Officers (JOs) have reported lack of adequate space in courtrooms.
        - **Low Spending:** 0.09% of GDP to maintain the judicial infrastructure.
        - **No Power Backup:** 59% of courtrooms
        - **Toilets:** 26% of court complexes do not have separate ladies toilets and 16% do not have gents’ toilets.
        - **Drinking water facility:** Only 54% of court complexes have purified drinking water facilities.
        - **Record room:** Only 32% of courtrooms have separate Record Rooms.
        - **Library:** Only 51% of court complexes have a library.
        - **Video-conference Facility**: Only 27% of courtrooms have computers placed on the Judge’s dais with video-conferencing facilities.
            - 50% of lawyers, particularly in district courts, do not have any laptop or computer facility

• Lok Adalat
- National Lok Adalat settles 1.45 crore cases, prevents 1.22 crore new cases (2024)

• Gram Nyayalayas
        - **Target: 2500**
        - **Limited implementation:** only 476 notified by just 15 states
        - **Operational: 314**
        - **No GN in North East**

• Fast Track Special Courts
- **745+ Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)**, including 404+ exclusive e-POCSO Courts, operational across 30 States/UTs (disposing >3.06 lakh cases) ([Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2295880®=6&lang=1))
        - collectively disposed of over 3,06,604 cases to date.
        - 1800 FTCs recommended by 14th Fin Commission

• Transparency Issues - Judges Asset Disclosure
- Out of 769 High Court judges, only 95 (12.35%) have publicly disclosed their assets.
- Kerala High Court leads with 18% of its judges disclosing assets (41 out of 44), followed closely by Himachal Pradesh at 91.66% (11 out of 12).
- Chhattisgarh HC (1/16) and Madras HC (5/65) report some of the lowest disclosures.
- As of April 2025, 30 of 33 SC judges have declared their assets, and a Full Court resolution ensures all 33 will publish their declarations soon.

Participation in Legislature

subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
content_markdown:
BIOTECHNOLOGY AND HEALTH SCIENCES

• Biotechnology
        - India is emerging as world leader in biotechnology
- Over **11,000+ biotech startups** (up from 6,500+) and 75+ bio-incubators supported by DBT/BIRAC; Union Budget 2026-27 also launched **Biopharma SHAKTI** with a ₹10,000 crore outlay over 5 years ([India BioEconomy Report 2026](https://ableindia.in/manage/images/resourceuploads/_IBER%202026_compressed.pdf) / [Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).
- India's **BioEconomy reached USD 195.3 billion in 2025** (up 18% from USD 165.7 billion in 2024 and USD 10 billion in 2014), contributing **nearly 5% (4.25–5%) to national GDP** and targeting $300 billion by 2030 ([BIRAC India BioEconomy Report 2026](https://ableindia.in/manage/images/resourceuploads/_IBER%202026_compressed.pdf))

• Human Genome Sequencing
        - India completed sequencing 10,000 healthy genomes from different regions, representing 99 distinct populations.

• Immunization (WHO Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) 2023)
        - **Global:**
            - Childhood immunization coverage stalled in 2023-> 2.7 million children either unvaccinated or under-vaccinated.
            - Over 50% of unvaccinated children live in the 31 conflict-affected countries.
            - **India:** In 2023, 1.6 million children missed crucial Diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus (together called DPT) and measles vaccinations.
            - India accounted for 2 million zero-dose children.
            - So far 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women have been vaccinated under Mission Indradhanush

• Neglected Tropical Diseases- Global report on Neglected Tropical Diseases 2024 (WHO)
        - **Global Burden:** Over 1 billion people affected by NTDs; 1.6 billion need preventive or curative interventions ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535)).
        - **India’s Share**: accounts for ~40% of the global population requiring NTD interventions—the highest worldwide.
        - **2030 Targets ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535)):**
            - 90% reduction in the number of people needing NTD interventions.
            - 75% reduction in vector-borne NTD-related deaths.
        - **Mortality Trend:** Deaths from vector-borne NTDs increased by 22% in 2022 compared to 2016.
        - **WASH Access:** 85.8% in NTD-endemic countries have WASH access overall, but only 63% among those needing NTD interventions.
        - **India’s Achievements:** Certified free of Guinea Worm (2000) and Yaws (2016) by WHO.
        - **Economic Cost:** Eliminating NTDs by 2030 could save over $342 billion in healthcare costs and productivity losses ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535)).

• Rare Diseases
        - In India, a disease is considered rare if it affects fewer than 1 in 2,500 individuals.
        - Over 70 million Indians living with rare diseases
        - 6,000-8,000 classified rare diseases, but < 5% have therapies available.
        - 95% rare diseases have no approved treatment & less than 1 in 10 patients receive disease-specific treatment.

• Non-communicable diseases
        - NCDs are **number 1 cause of death** and disability worldwide -> 74% of all deaths
        - **low- and middle-income countries-**> 77 percent of all NCD deaths occurred.
        - **Four top killers -**> cardiovascular diseases (17·9 million), cancers (9.3 million), chronic respiratory diseases (4.1 million), and diabetes (2.0 million). ### Section Group: Frontier Technologies & IPR

R&D AND IPR

• Gross expenditure on R&D (GERD)
        - **Gross expenditure on R&D (GERD)** ↑ from ₹60,196 crore in FY11 to about ₹1,27,381 crore in FY21.
        - Central Government (43.7%), State Governments (6.7%), Higher Education (8.8%) & Public Sector Industry (4.4%).

        - **Women participation:** In extramural R&D projects has increased significantly to 25% in 2019–20 from 13% in 2000–01.

• Research output
        - **Research output:** India is world’s 4th in research output, but ranks 9th in citations
        - India strong in chemistry research, with the subject making up almost 60% of its total Nature Index output.
        - India aims to overtake US in the number of scientific publications by 2029

• Patent applications
- **Patent applications:** Surged to **1,43,729 patent applications filed in FY 2025-26** (and **1,10,375 in FY 2024-25**, up from 58,503 in FY 2020-21; placing India in the **global Top 6 for patent filings**) ([MeitY](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2291148®=48&lang=2) / [CGPDTM](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2260532®=6&lang=1) / [PIB May 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2260532®=6&lang=1)).

• Patent grants
- **Patent grants:** Over **1,03,057 (one lakh+) patents granted in FY24** (up nearly 17-fold from 5,978 in 2014-15) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [CGPDTM](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2260532®=6&lang=1))
        - **Term of Patent**: Every patent granted is 20 years from the date of filing of the application.

• Disposal of patent application
        - **Disposal of patent application:** In India, it takes about 58 months on average to dispose of a patent application ( 20 months in China and 23 months in US).

• Global rank
- **Global rank (GII):** India ranks **38th out of 139 economies in the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025 and GII 2026** (up from 39th in GII 2024 and 81st in 2015; ranks **1st among 36 lower-middle-income economies** and 1st globally in ICT services exports) ([WIPO GII 2026](https://www.wipo.int/gii-ranking/en/india))
- **Global rank (IP Index):** India ranked 42nd–43rd out of 55 economies in the International Intellectual Property Index ([US Chamber of Commerce GIPC 2024/2025](https://www.uschamber.com/intellectual-property/2025-ip-index))
        - **Low student enrollment** in advanced programs (total enrolment in Ph.D. stood at 2.12 lakh in 2021-22- as per All India Survey on Higher Education).
        - **PhDs Produced**: India annually awards 40,813 PhDs, ranking third globally, after the United States and China.
        - **Future Prospects**: India to spend at least 1%, but ideally 3%, of its GDP every year until 2047 on R&D for science to have a meaningful impact on development.

SPACE TECHNOLOGY

• Space economy
        - **India:** Current size: $8.4 billion (around 2-3% of global space economy); expected to reach $44 billion by 2033.
        - **Global:** $570 billion
        - **Funding:** ↓ 55% to $59.1 mn in 2024 (Tracxn data)

• ISRO
- **Annual budget:** ~₹13,416 crore (~$1.6 billion in Union Budget 2025-26 / 2026-27, plus ₹1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund for space startups approved under IN-SPACe) ([Department of Space](https://www.isro.gov.in/))
        - **Low cost:** India spent $74m on the Mars orbiter Mangalyaan and $75m on last year’s historic Chandrayaan-3 – less than the $100m spent on the sci-fi thriller Gravity!!
- **Space docking (SpaDeX, Jan 2025):** India became the **4th country** (after the US, Russia, and China) to achieve autonomous satellite space docking via ISRO's SpaDeX mission ([ISRO](https://www.isro.gov.in/) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).

• Private sector in space
- Over **250+ space startups** are now active in India, leveraging ISRO and IN-SPACe facilities ([Department of Space](https://www.isro.gov.in/) / [IN-SPACe](https://www.inspace.gov.in/))
        - Total funding raised -> fell 35% YoY to $81 Mn last year (Inc42’s Indian Startup Funding Report 2024)

• Space tourism
        - **Global space tourism market size:** USD 851.4 million in 2023 ; projected to reach USD 8,669.2 million by 2030
        - Travel to the International Space Station (ISS) is estimated to cost between 20 to 25 million dollars.

• Space debris
        - **India:** By 2030, all Indian satellites will be launched under the zero orbital debris mission.
        - **Global:** 40,000 objects larger than 10 cm, with millions of smaller fragments

NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY

• Global rank
    - India ranks 7th in terms of the number of nuclear reactors.
    - 5th largest source of electricity for India
    - 25 operable nuclear energy reactors
- Total installed capacity of **8.78–8.88 GW (8,780–8,880 MW)** across 25 operable nuclear reactors as of March 2026 ([DAE](https://dae.gov.in/) / [MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
    - target of 100 GW nuclear power capacity by 2047
    - Nuclear power generation capacity doubled from 4,780 MW in 2014 to 8,180 MW in 2024
- Union Budget 2025-26 announced **₹20,000 crore for the Nuclear Energy Mission** (targeting 5 indigenous Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) by 2033 and 100 GW by 2047); **Union Budget 2026-27 extended basic customs duty exemption on imports for Nuclear Power Projects till 2035** ([Union Budget 2025-26](https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/union-budget-2025-26-analysis) & 2026-27).

• India's three-stage nuclear power programme
    - **India's three-stage nuclear power programme (by Dr Homi Bhabha in the 1950s):**
        - **Stage 1**: Natural Uranium Fuelled Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)
        - **Stage 2**: Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs) Utilizing Plutonium-Based Fuel
        - **Stage 3**: Advanced Nuclear Power Systems for Utilization of Thorium

• Others
    - First uranium deposit in India was found in 1951 at Jaduguda, in the Singhbhum Thrust Belt (Jharkhand).
    - **Operational Costing**: Estimates show that nuclear plants cost only 33-50% of a coal plant and 20-25% of a gas combined-cycle plant.

content_markdown:
HUNGER, POVERTY & INEQUALITY

• Poverty

• India - Poverty
        - **Percentage**: 21.9% {2011, Tendulkar Report}
- **Extreme poverty:** Under the World Bank's revised International Poverty Line ($3.00/day at 2021 PPP, up from $2.15/day), India's extreme poverty rate stood at **5.3% in 2022-23** (and 23.9% at the lower-middle-income line) [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]
        - **Decrease in Poverty [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]**
            - **Extreme Poverty Lift:** 171 Million lifted from Extreme Poverty in last decade.
            - **India’s Poverty Rate** (at the 3.65 dollars per day line)-> Fell from 61.8 percent in 2011-12 to 28.1 percent in 2022-23.
                - **Rural poverty** declined from 69 percent to 32.5 percent
                - **Urban poverty** dropped from 43.5 percent to 17.2 percent.
- **Non-monetary poverty (Multidimensional Poverty Index - MPI)** -> declined from 55.3% in 2005-06 to **11.28% in 2022-23** (24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty in 9 years) ([NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) [[UNDP](https://hdr.undp.org/) MPI: 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21].

• Global - Poverty
        - **Incidence**: 8.5% of total population i.e. 75 cr live in extreme poverty - on less than $2.15 per day [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]
        - **Deprived Regions:** 5 out of 6 poor are in Sub-Saharan or South Asia
        - **Rural > Urban** – over 75% of all poor live in rural areas.
        - **High Prevalence among Children (< 18):** 50% of total poor

• Inequality
- **Oxfam Report - Global**
    - The richest 1% control 45% of global wealth.
- **Oxfam Report - India**
    - Richest 1% control more than 40% of total wealth
    - Bottom 50% own merely 3%
- **Gini Coefficient**
    - The Gini coefficient improved for rural areas (declined to 0.237 in 2023-24 from 0.266 in 2022-23) and urban areas (declined to 0.284 in 2023-24 from 0.314 in 2022- 23).
- **Rural-Urban Divide:** Average Monthly Per Capita Expenditure (MPCE) -> Rs. 4, 122 (Rural) and Rs. 6,996 (Urban) ([Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports)).

• Hunger
- **Status of Hunger [[Global Hunger Index 2024](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]**
    - **Global**
        - 2.8 billion people cannot afford a healthy diet.
    - **India Specific**
- **India's Rank:** Improved to **102nd out of 123 countries in Global Hunger Index 2025** (up from 105th out of 127 in GHI 2024; remains in the "serious" category) [[GHI 2025](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]
        - **Child Wasting Rate**: 18.7% [Highest in World]
- **Stunted Children**: **32.9% in GHI 2025** (29.3% in UN SDR 2026; down from >35% earlier; Child Wasting at 18.7%) [[GHI 2025](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]
        - **Under-5 mortality**: 2.9%
- **Status of Food Security [[State of Food Security and Nutrition Report (2024)](https://www.fao.org/publications/home/fao-flagship-publications/the-state-of-food-security-and-nutrition-in-the-world)]**
    - **India Specific**
        - **Undernourished**: 13% from Chronic Undernourishment
        - **Anemic**: 53% of Women
- **UN-FAO Report**
    - Hunger in India came down to **13.7%** during 2021-23 period ### Section Group: Social Sector & Human Development

subject: SOCIAL JUSTICE
content_markdown:
HEALTH

• Mental Health
        - **India**
            - **Lifetime prevalence** of mental disorders in India is 13.7%.
            - 10.6% of adults in India suffer from mental disorders (National Mental Health Survey (NMHS) 2015-16)
            - **Mental Health in Students**
                - 23% of school children have mental health problems (NIMHANS study)
                - 27.8% of undergraduate students had mentalhealth conditions and 31.3 per cent of postgraduate students had suicidal thoughts.
            - **Self-reporting rate**: <1% (IIT Jodhpur study)
            - **Treatment gap:** 70-92%
            - **Economic Loss:** B/w 2012-2030, is estimated at USD 1.03 trillion ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535))
            - **Mental health professionals**
                - Only 0.75 psychiatrists, 0.07 psychologists and 0.07 social workers per 1 lakh people.
                - India short of 27,000 psychiatrists to reach the recommended ratio of 3 per 1 lakh people.
- **Mental healthcare budget & initiatives**: Govt spends ~0.05% of GDP (~1.1% of health budget) on mental health; **Union Budget 2026-27 announced setting up NIMHANS-2 in North India** and upgrading National Mental Health Institutes in Ranchi and Tezpur as Regional Apex Institutions ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).
        - **Global**
            - 13.9% of population experience mental disorders
            - India (0.75 psychiatrists per lakh people) vs Developed countries (6.6 psychiatrists per 100,000 people).

• Traditional Medicines
        - **India**
            - **Medicinal plants market**-> Rs. 4.2 billion in 2019; expected to increase at CAGR of 38.5% to Rs. 14 billion by 2030.
- 8,000 herbal remedies codified in AYUSH systems; **Union Budget 2026-27 announced 3 new All India Institutes of Ayurveda** (Ministry of AYUSH / [Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).
            - **Ayush exports:** $18 billion
        - **Global**
            - 80% of the population use traditional medicine.
            - Global herbal medicine market is projected to grow from $153.5 billion in 2022 to $279.8 billion in 2028.

• Tobacco Consumption
        - **India**
            - 2nd largest consumer and producer of tobacco
            - **Usage:** 42% of men and 14% of women in India use tobacco (GATS2 data)
            - **Deaths:** In India, nearly 3600 people die every day due to tobacco use.
            - **Economic loss**
                - India loses 1% of its GDP to diseases and early deaths from tobacco use ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535))
                - For every Rs 100 received as excise taxes from tobacco products, the economy loses Rs 816.
            - **Wastage:** 1.7 lakh tonnes of waste every year.
        - **Global**
            - 1 in every 10 cigarettes and tobacco products consumed globally is illicit.
            - 22.3% of the world's population used tobacco ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535))

• Rural Health
        - There is shortage of 83.2% of surgeons, 74.2% of obstetricians and gynaecologists, 79.1% of physicians, 81.6% of paediatricians in rural areas.
        - Only 45.1% PHCs function on a 24×7 basis.
        - Of the 5,480 functioning CHCs, only 541 have all four specialists.

EDUCATION

• Brain Drain
        - B/w 2015 and 2022, 1.3 million Indians left.
        - **Citizenship renounced:** 225,000 Indians renounced their citizenship (2022).
        - **Economic loss:** India’s IT industry could have added $15-20 billion more annually had the talent stayed.
        - 75% of emigrating Indians choose to stay back after studies completion.

• Exam Leaks
        - 70 exam leaks in the last 7 years across 15 states.

WOMEN

• Social Issues

• CRIMES (Marital Rape)
        - 2% of married women face physical, sexual or emotional violence by their husbands.
        - India is one of only 36 countries where marital rape is not criminalized.

VULNERABLE SECTIONS

• Child Marriage
- 23.3% of women aged 20–24 years were married before age 18 in NFHS-5 (2019-21); as per **SRS Statistical Report 2024**, the mean age at effective marriage for females rose to **23.1 years**, with only **2.1% of females marrying before age 18** in 2024 ([ORGI SRS 2024](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf)).
        - 17.7% of men aged 25-29 years were married before age 21 years.
        - Prevalence reduced by half from 47% (2006) to 23.3% (2019-21).
        - Total cases registered under Child Marriage Act -> 1050 (2021) ([NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/)).
        - Every minute, three girls are forced into child marriage ['India Child Protection' research team study].

• Child Artist
        - B/w 6,059 and 12,334 child artists [Study by Child Rights and You].
        - Child artists in films and TV work for over 12 hours a day.

content_markdown:
EDUCATION

• School Enrollment

• At School Level
- **Children in Schools**: **24.69 crore students across 14.71 lakh schools**, supported by **>1.01 crore teachers** (with GER at 90.9 in Primary, 90.3 in Upper Primary, 78.7 in Secondary, and 58.4 in Higher Secondary) [[UDISE+ 2024-25](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2219907) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)] (24.80 crore in UDISE+ 2023-24)
        - **Private Schools Enrollment:** 36% (9 crore) of total school enrolment [[UDISE+ 2023-24 data](https://udiseplus.gov.in/)]
        - **Schools**
            - **Government Schools:** 38.11% (27.8 lakh)
            - **Unaided Schools:** 60.75% (44.31 lakh)
            - **School Enrolment**:↓ 37 lakh in 2023-24 compared to previous year [[UDISE data](https://udiseplus.gov.in/)].

• Higher Education Level
        - **Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) ->** 0.4 in 1950-51 to 28.4 in 2021-22.
        - **Student Enrolment:** Over 4 crore students, making India the second- largest after China.
        - **Target for GER**: National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 aims for 50% by 2035
        - World **2nd Largest** Higher Education system
        - **Girls with Higher Education**: Enrolment of women in Indian universities grew 26% in 2024.
        - **Vulnerable Sections**: Enrollment among OBCs increased by 80.9%, SC enrollment grew by 76.3%.
        - **Stream wise Ratio**:
            - Humanities (33%), Science (15%), Commerce (14%), English (12%)
        - **Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR)**: Steady at 23:1 for the last five years.
        - **University Density (per 1 lakh eligible students):** Highest in Sikkim (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (5.6), Ladakh (5.2), etc. In Bihar (0.2), UP (0.3), West Bengal & Maharashtra (0.6) the density is below national average.

• Expenditure
- **Government Spending:**
    - **Expenditure**: 2.9% of GDP
    - **Target under NEP 2020**: 6% of GDP
- **Budgetary allocation (2026-27):** **₹1.39 lakh crore (₹1,39,289.48 crore)** allocated to the Ministry of Education in Union Budget 2026-27 (including ₹83,562 crore for School Education and ₹55,727 crore for Higher Education), an **8.27% hike** over ₹1.28 lakh crore in 2025-26 ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).

• Infrastructure
- **Inefficient Infrastructure [[UDISE+ 2023-24 Report](https://udiseplus.gov.in/)]**
    - **Computers:** The percentage of schools having computers ↑ from 38.5 % in 2019-20 to 57.2 % in 2023-2024.
    - **Internet:** Percentage of schools having internet facility increased from 22.3 % in 2019-20 to 53.9 % in 2023-2024.
    - **Electricity:** Of the over 14.71 lakh schools in India, up to 1.52 lakh schools have no functional electricity.
    - **Drinking Water**: While 14.47 lakh schools claim to have drinking water facilities, only 14.11 lakh have them functional.
    - **Toilets**: Government schools constitute the majority of the 67,000 schools operating without functional toilets.
    - **Differently-Abled Students:** Only 33.2% of government schools have disabled-friendly toilets.
    - **Digital Education**: 46 % schools have functional computers ([Ministry of Education](https://www.education.gov.in/))

• Institutions
- **Universities and Colleges:**
- **Institutions:** Total Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) increased from 51,534 in 2014-15 to **70,018 as of June 2025** (with **23 IITs, 21 IIMs, and 20 AIIMS**, plus 2 international IIT campuses in Zanzibar and Abu Dhabi) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) [1,168 universities, 45,473 colleges, and 12,002 stand-alone institutions in AISHE 2021-22].
    - **Accreditation**: Only 37% of universities are accredited
    - **Growth**: In last 10 years, number of universities has increased by 60%, colleges up 21% [[Ministry of Education](https://www.education.gov.in/)]
    - **Increased Penetration in Rural Areas:** 43% Universities and 61.4% colleges are located in Rural Areas.
    - **Institutes of National Importance (INIs)**: 171 [June 2024]
    - **Medical Colleges:** 102% increase-> rising from 387 before 2014 to 780 in 2024
        - **Increase in MBBS seats:** 130% rise in MBBS seats
    - **IIMs:** 21
    - **IITs:** 23

• Startup
- **Definition:** An entity, HQ in India, opened less than 10 years ago, and annual turnover < ₹100 crore.
- **Recognized startups:** DPIIT-recognized startups increased from ~500 (2016) to **over 2.23 lakh as of 31 March 2026** (up from 1.59 lakh in early 2025) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB April 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)).
- **Positive Ecosystem:** 3rd largest startup ecosystem in India
- **High Failure Rate:** 90% fail within 5 years.
- **Employment Generation:** Recognized startups have created **over 23.36 lakh direct jobs as of 31 March 2026** (up from 16.6 lakh in Oct 2024) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB April 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)).
- **Women Entrepreneurship:** **Over 1.07 lakh recognized startups** have at least one woman director/partner as of 31 March 2026 (~48% of total recognized startups, up from 73,151) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB April 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)).

• Higher Education: Pain Points
- Only 42.6% of Indian graduates are employable [India's Graduate Skill Index 2025]
- **QS World Rankings 2025:** Top Indian Institutes
    - **No Institute in TOP 100**
    - **IIT Bombay**: Leading in India, IIT Bombay climbed from 149th in 2024 to 118th in 2025.
    - **IIT Delhi:** Achieved the second position in India, moving up 47 ranks from 197th to 150th.
- **Schools:**
    - **ASER 2024**
        - **Reading skill:** 76.6% of Class 3 students still cannot read Class 2 text.
        - **Foundational Numeracy Skills**
            - Over 50% of students (14-18 age) face difficulties with elementary division problems.
        - **Arithmetic**
            - 66.3% of Class 3 students and 70% of Class 5 students cannot perform simple arithmetic calculations.
            - Class 3 students able to do subtraction is just 33.7% in 2024.
- **Vocational Training**
    - Only about 2% have received formal vocational training [Ministry of Skill Development]
- **Problem in Basic Skills:**
    - NCERT **Report 2022**
        - 11% of Class 3 students in India lack basic skills in Mathematics.

• Skilling
- **Level of Skill Training:** <5% of people are formally skilled (> 20% is china, > 50% in USA, 95% is South Korea)
- **Low Formal Training**: only 2.7% of India’s workforce has received formal skill training, compared to 52% in US, 80% in Japan, and 96% in South Korea.
