content_markdown:
HEALTH

• Health GDP%
- **Government Spending:**
- ~1.84–1.9% of GDP (Union Budget 2026-27 increased allocation for Ministry of Health & Family Welfare by 10% to **₹1,06,530.42 crore** for FY 2026-27) ([Economic Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf) / [Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455))
    - World Average = 6%
    - Target = 2.5% [National Health Policy, 2017]
- **Economic Survey (2024-25)**
    - **Share of government health spending in total health expenditure** increased to 48 per cent in 2022 from 29 per cent in 2015.
    - In FY 2022, India spent ₹9.04 lakh crore on health—3.8% of GDP-> ₹6,602 per person.

• Health of Poverty
- **Out of Pocket Expenditure (OoPE):**
    - **Decrease in OoPE:** OOPE as a percentage of total health expenditure (THE) declined from 62.6% in 2014-15 to 39.4% in 2021-22 [[National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates](https://nhsrcindia.org/national-health-accounts-records)]
    - **People Pushed into Poverty:** 6 crore people pushed into poverty every year, due to OoPE [[NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf)]

• Human Resource
- **Availability of Doctors and Nurse:**
    - **Public Sector**: Only 10% of doctors are in the Public Sector.
    - **Doctor/Population:** 1: 834 v/s 1: 1000 ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535) recommended)
        - 112% increase in MBBS seats (since 2014)
        - Allopathic doctors to population — 1 doctor/1,194 people.
    - **Nurse/Population Ratio:** 1.96 per 1,000 [[WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535) recommended 3 per 1,000]

• Infra/Inputs
- **Bed: Patient:** 1.3/1000 v/s 3: 1000
    - Delhi: 2.7/1000
- **Increase in Colleges:** 82% increase in Medical Colleges (since 2014)
- **Institutional deliveries [[MoHFW](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2246870®=1&lang=1)]**
- ↑ from 79% (NFHS-4, 2015-16) to **88.6% (~89%) in NFHS-5 (2019-21)**, and further to **95.4% of deliveries receiving medical attention in 2024** [[MoHFW](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2246870®=1&lang=1) / [ORGI SRS Statistical Report 2024](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf)].
    - 100% in Kerala, Goa, Lakshadweep, Puducherry and Tamil Nadu and more than 90% in eighteen other States/UTs.
- **Import Dependency:**
    - **Active Pharma Ingredients** (API)
        - 70-80% imported from China
        - Indian API market projected to reach $21.2 billion by 2033.
    - **Medical Equipments**: ~ 75% are imported

• Insurance

• Insurance Penetration
        - **Low Insurance Penetration**: 3.7% in FY24 [Global average: 7%]
            - **Life Insurance penetration**: dropped marginally from 3 % in FY23 to 2.8 % in FY24 [[Economic Survey 2024–25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)]
            - **Non-life insurance** remained at 1%.
        - India ranks **10th** in the global life insurance market.

• Insurance Coverage
        - **Health Insurance**: 37% covered under Health Insurance Schemes.
        - **Without Health Insurance**: 90 crore Indians lack access to health Insurance [[IRDAI data](https://irdai.gov.in/annual-reports)]

• Health Insurance Sector
        - **Market size:** 6th largest insurance market by 2032 ([Swiss Re report](https://www.swissre.com/institute/research/sigma-research/sigma-2026-01-natcat-2025-wildfire-storm-risk.html))
        - **Density:** $91 insurance density (global avg $874)
- **Insurance Premium:** Total insurance premium grew from ₹8.3 lakh crore in FY21 and ₹11.2 lakh crore in FY24 to **₹11.9 lakh crore in FY25** ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))

• Rural Areas Variations
- **Rural Areas**: ≈ 20% of Total Hospital
- **Shortage of Manpower in Rural Areas [[Union Ministry of Health data](https://mohfw.gov.in/)]**
    - **Doctors:** 70% shortage of specialist doctors
    - **Primary Health Centres:** Shortfall of 3.1% of allopathic doctors ([Rural Health Statistics 2021-2022](https://mohfw.gov.in/))
    - **Rural Community Health Centres:** maximum for surgeons (73 per cent) followed by physicians (69 per cent), paediatricians (68 per cent) and Obs & Gyn specialists (61 per cent)

• Disease Burden
- **Non communicable disease:** 2/3rd of total deaths
    - 5.8 million Indians die from NCDs each year
    - 1 in 4 Indians faces the risk of dying from NCD before reaching age of 70.
- **TB:** 26.07 lakh TB cases in 2024, marking highest notified cases ever.
- **India among 10 countries** that make up 60 % of global maternal deaths, still births, new born deaths (UN)
- **Mortality Rate [Sample Registration System (SRS) Statistical Report 2024 (released May 2026) & 2021-23 Bulletin]**
- **MMR:** **88–93 per lakh live births** (reduced by 86% since 1990, outpacing the global 48% reduction; 93 in SRS 2019-21) ([ORGI SRS](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **NMR:** **18–19 per 1,000 live births** (70% decline during 1990–2023 vs 54% globally) ([ORGI SRS](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **IMR:** Declined to **24 per 1,000 live births in 2024** (down from 25 in 2023, 27 in 2021, and 40 in 2013; lowest in Kerala at 8) ([ORGI SRS Statistical Report 2024](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf))
- **U5MR:** Declined to **28 per 1,000 live births in 2024** (down from 29 in 2023 and 31 in 2021; 78% reduction since 1990 vs 61% globally) ([ORGI SRS Statistical Report 2024](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf))
- **Anaemia ([NFHS 5](https://mohfw.gov.in/)):**
    - 2/3 or 67% of children
    - 1/2 or 57% of women
    - 1/4 or 25% of Men
    - 3 in 4 Indian women have low dietary iron intake.

• Obesity
- **India**: 3rd most obese country
    - **Urban** – 70% of Obese people
- **1/4 Indian** is Obese ([NFHS 5](https://mohfw.gov.in/))
    - 22.9% of men and 24% of women are obese.
    - % of overweight children under five increased to 3.4% from 2.1% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) at the all-India level.
- **Definition:** WHO defines it as abnormal fat accumulation with:
    - BMI > 30 -> Obese
    - BMI 25-30 -> Overweight
- **Economic cost:** USD 28.95 billion (Rs 1,800 per capita)
    - By 2030 ↑ to Rs 4,700 per capita or 1.57% of GDP.
- **Global**
    - One-third of children worldwide will be obese by 2050 [Lancet Study]
    - 211 crore obese individuals in 2021 (45% of the world’s population).

• Open Defecation
- **Lack of Toilet Access:** 20% do not have access to toilet {1 in 5 household practice open deficiency} – NFHS 5
- **World Bank** – 11 % of India’s Population practice open defecation.

VULNERABLE SECTIONS

• Child {0-18 yrs.}
- **Population**:
    - 1/3rd of country population
    - 40-45 Cr
    - 19% of the World's children

- **Child beggars**: 3 lac
- **Missing:** 1 child is missing every 8 mins
- **Child labour**
    - 10.1 million children, or 3.9% of the total child population, are "main workers" or "marginal workers" ([Census 2011](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/))
    - In rural areas, 13.9% of children are involved in child labor, compared to 4.7% in urban areas.
    - 70% of child laborers are in agriculture, 20% in services, and 10% in industry.
- **Cybercrime:** Child cyber crimes surges 32% compared to previous year ([NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/))
- **Malnutrition**
    - **Child Wasting Rate**: 18.7% [Highest in World]
- **Stunted Children**: **32.9% in GHI 2025** (down from 35.5% in [NFHS-5](https://mohfw.gov.in/)) ([GHI 2025](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf) / [NFHS-5](https://mohfw.gov.in/))
    - **Under-5 mortality**: 2.9%
    - **Undernourished**: 13% from Chronic Undernourishment
    - **Anemic**: 1 in every 3

• Elderly
- **Population (Elderly 60+)**: 10.38 cr (8.6% in [Census 2011](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/)) -> rose to **9.7% of total population in 2024** ([SRS Statistical Report 2024](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf)) and ~10.1–11% (~14+ cr) in 2025, projected to reach ~20% by 2050 ([UNFPA India Ageing Report](https://india.unfpa.org/en/publications/india-ageing-report-2023))
- **Growth**: Expected to rise to 20% in 2050
- **Sex ratio:** 1033 {2011} -> Feminisation of Ageing
- **Growth Rate** ≈ 3%

• Disabled
- **Population:** 2.68 crore ([Census 2011](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/))
    - 2.3% of India's population was reported as having some form of disability.
        - 2.3% in rural areas
        - 2% in urban areas.
- **Reservation**:
    - 4% Reservation is Government Jobs
    - 5% is higher education.
- **Economic Cost:** India loses approximately Rs 4.5 lakh crore annually - about 4% of its GDP - due to the exclusion of disabled ([Economic Survey 2023](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2023-24/economicsurvey/index.php))

• Trans Genders
- **Population**: 4.88 lakh ([Census 2011](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/))
- **Mental health issues:** 31% attempted suicide.
- **Gender Discrimination**: 27% were denied care due to gender identity (NALSA)

• Minorities
- 18% of the population

• SC
- **Population**: 16.6%
- **Literacy Rate**: 66%
- **Reservation**: 15%

• ST
- **Population**: 8.6%
- **Literary Rate**: 59%
- **Reservation**: 7.5%
- 705 notified tribes | Meghalaya (Lowest)
- **Atrocities**: ~67,000+ cases of atrocities against SCs and STs in 2022–2023; in 2024, crimes against SCs decreased by 3.6% and crimes against STs declined by 23.1% over 2023, while crimes against Senior Citizens rose by 16.9% ([NCRB Crime in India 2024](https://ncrb.gov.in/crime-in-india.html))

• OBC
- **Population**: 52%
- **Reservation**: 27%

• Miscellaneous
- **Gen Z population - India**
- Largest Gen Z population in the world (377 million individuals)
- **Workforce:** By 2025, Gen Z is projected to comprise 27.3% of India's workforce.
- **Collective spending** is at $860 billion (43% of total consumption in country).
    - Projected to hit $2 trillion by 2035
- **Loneliness**: 61% Gen Z believe people are more lonely today than they were 10 years ago, (Spotify Culture Next Report 2024).

WOMEN

• Economic Empowerment

• Wage Gap
        - Indian women earn Rs 40 for every Rs 100 men earn ([WEF](https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_GGGR_Report_2026.pdf))
- **India rank**: **131st out of 145 countries in Global Gender Gap Index 2026** (parity score **64.5%**; was 131st out of 148 countries with 64.1–64.4% score in GGGI 2025) ([WEF Global Gender Gap Report 2026](https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_GGGR_Report_2026.pdf))

• Labor Force Participation
        - **India**: The female LFPR has risen from 23.3 %(2017- 18) to 41.7%(2023-24). **([Eco survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)).**
        - **Global:** Women's global labour force participation rate stood at 48.7 per cent in 2023 **([ILO](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/@dgreports/@dcomm/@publ/documents/publication/wcms_711919.pdf)).**

• Women in Informal Sector
        - More than 95% women working in Informal sector ([ILO](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/@dgreports/@dcomm/@publ/documents/publication/wcms_711919.pdf))

• Finance Availability to Women
        - 80% of women run enterprises are self-financed
        - < 5% borrowed money from some financial institutions.

• Global Gender Gap Report 2025 & 2026 (WEF)
- **India's Gender Parity Score**: **64.5% in 2026** (vs global average of **69.2%**; India scored 96.6% in Educational Attainment, 95.6% in Health & Survival, 41.2% in Economic Participation, and 24.5% in Political Empowerment) [64.1–64.4% in 2025] ([WEF GGGR 2026](https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_GGGR_Report_2026.pdf))
- **India rank:** **131/145 in GGGR 2026** (131/148 in GGGR 2025) ([WEF GGGR 2026](https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_GGGR_Report_2026.pdf))
- **South Asia**: Bhutan (119), Nepal (125), and Sri Lanka (130) ranked better than India.
- **Gender Parity Timeline:** At the current pace, it will take **~120 years** globally to achieve full gender parity in GGGR 2026 (down from 134 years earlier) ([WEF GGGR 2026](https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_GGGR_Report_2026.pdf)).

• Social Issues

• Education
        - **Literary Rate**: 65.46% ([2011 Census](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/))
        - **Worldwide:** 12.2 crore girls remain out of school globally [[UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/india/)]
        - **Gender Parity in Secondary Education**: India showed the best gender parity in terms of enrolment in secondary education [[Global Gender Gap report, 2024](https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_GGGR_2025.pdf)]

• Health (NFHS-5)
- **TFR:** **2.0 in NFHS-5 (2019-21)** and declined further to **1.9 in SRS Statistical Report 2024** (below replacement level of 2.1) ([NFHS-5](https://mohfw.gov.in/) / [ORGI SRS 2024](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/47152/download/51396/SRS_STAT_2024.pdf))
- **Anaemia**: **57% of women aged 15–49 years** are anaemic in India ([NFHS-5](https://mohfw.gov.in/)) [~1 in 3 globally]

• CRIMES
        - India records **51 cases** of crime against women every hour ([NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/))
        - 1/3rd crimes by husband/relative ([MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1767781372753_1380ce82-f5a5-440d-99e6-e6b35af0deb5_GDP_Press_Note_on_FAE_2025-26.pdf))
        - **Cybercrime**: reporting surged by 25%
        - **Suicides**: 4.2% Increase ([NCRB, 2022](https://ncrb.gov.in/crime-in-india.html))
        - **Rape**
            - 4th most common crime against women
            - India lodged average 86 rapes daily: NCRB data

• Others (Demographic)
        - **Median age:** 28.2 years **(**China -> 38 yrs)
        - **Sex Ratio:** 1020 ([NFHS -5](https://mohfw.gov.in/))
        - **CSR:** 929 (from 919) ([NFHS - 5](https://mohfw.gov.in/))

• Political Representation
- 18th L.S -> 13.6% (17th LS -> 14.4%)
    - World Average (25%); Rwanda: 61%; SA: 43%; UK: 32%; USA: 24%
- **Women as MLAs**: 9%
- **Women in Local Bodies**: 33% reservation but more than 40% representation
- **Women in legislative bodies [Since Independence]**
    - **Lok Sabha:** 22 (5%) in 1951 -> 74 (13.6%) in 2024.
    - **Rajya Sabha**: 7% in 1952 -> 13% in 2023.

• Political Participation
        - Women voters -> 50%
        - **Female Voter turnout**
            - 65.8% during the 18th Lok Sabha Elections.

• Women & STEM
- **India**: 43% of STEM graduates are women but only 14% stem jobs are with women.
    - Women currently represent only 26% of the workforce in data science and artificial intelligence (AI).
- **Global**: Women make for 35% STEM graduates globally [[UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/)]

• Others
- **Women & Unpaid work**: 2/3rd {Men: 1/4th)
- **Women & GDP**
    - **Indian women:** contribute only 18% to GDP [[National Family Health Survey](https://mohfw.gov.in/)] vs **Global Avg.** = 45%
    - **Advancing women's equality ->**
        - Boost global GDP by $28 trillion and
        - add $770 billion to India’s GDP by 2025.
- **Women @ Board Level**: 28.7% share in board of directors in FY25.
- **Women & Assets**: Own 2% of total assets
- **Women led Startup**: > 7,000 active women-led startups, making up 7.5% of all active startups in the country [Tracxn report].
- **Women & SHGs**: Over 10.05 crore rural women households mobilized into 90.90+ lakh SHGs under DAY-NRLM; additionally, **over 31 crore unorganised workers are registered on e-Shram (54% women)** as of Jan 2026, and **55.02 crore PMJDY accounts (~56% women)** as of Mar 2025 [[MoRD](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2201070®=3&lang=1) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]
- **Women and Financial Inclusion**[[MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1767781372753_1380ce82-f5a5-440d-99e6-e6b35af0deb5_GDP_Press_Note_on_FAE_2025-26.pdf)].
    - **Bank accounts:** Women own 39.2% of all bank accounts in India, with rural areas seeing an even higher participation rate at 42.2%.
    - **Bank deposits**: Women contribute 39.7% to total bank deposits. ### Section Group: Urbanisation

content_markdown:
URBANIZATION

• Population
- **World population:** ~57% of global population lives in urban areas (UN World Urbanization Prospects / [World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india))
- **Population (India Urban Share)**: 31.16% (37.7 crore) in Census 2011 -> ~36.4% (~52+ crore) in 2024–2025 -> projected to reach ~40% (~60 crore) by 2036 ([Census 2011](https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/) / [World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india) / [MoHUA](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526))
    - Increase of 40% by 2036 – World Bank
- **GDP contribution** = 63%
    - Increase to 70% by 2036 – World Bank
- **Growth Rate:** India urban population for 2022 was 50.8 Cr, a 2.05% increase from 2021 ([World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)).

• Slums
- **Census 2011 - Total Population in Slums:** 6.55 cr Indians live in Slums (around 5%)
    - Maharashtra (1.18 cr) > Andhra Pradesh (1.02 cr)
- **Cities with >10 Lakh Population:** over 29% population living in slums (EPW).
    - Bombay (over 34%, Calcutta 32%, Madras 32% and Delhi 31%).
    - 65% of Indian cities have adjoining slums.

• Homeless
- **Census 2011** - 0.15% of population (17-18 lac)
- **Commissioners of SC -** 1% of the urban population is homeless (~37 lakhs).
- **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs:** approx 23.93 lakh people are homeless.

• Migration
- **Total Migration Rate** = 28.9% ([Migration in India report, 2020-21](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports))
    - **Rural Areas** - 26.5 %
    - **Urban Areas -** 34.9%
    - **Employment: 10.8%** persons were migrated for employment related reasons
    - **Females:** 47.9% - (48% in rural and 47.8% in urban areas)
        - **Main reason – Marriage:** 86.8% females migrated for marriage
    - **Males:** 10.7% - (5.9% in rural and 22.5% in urban areas)
        - **Main reason – Employment:** 49.6% of males migrated for employment
- **Domestic migrants:** ↓ 12% to 40.20 crore between 2011 and 2023 [[EAC-PM](https://eacpm.gov.in/)].

• Miscellaneous
- **Open Defecation:** Over 25% rural households defecate in the open in contrast to Swachh Bharat data ([NFHS-5](https://mohfw.gov.in/))
- **Electricity:**
    - **Households**: 97% of households have electricity
- **World Bank** – 100% of Urban Population has access to electricity.
